Hello Valtteri!

I agree that such cases should be taken as safety on condition that the driver indeed was using the car in an unsafe manner. It is difficult to unify the approach as it has to be taken case by case, but the overall advice is: 

* If the road conditions require the car to have winter tires and car was running on summer ones, and if the passenger noticed it during the ride (the car swerved, the braking was too long but the driver didn’t have any car collisions), it should be taken as Use of Unsafe Vehicle.
* If the driver collided with another car, the case should be taken as one of the Collision-related event categories. 
* If the weather was warm and the road surface was clean, so no incident happened at all, and the country doesn’t require drivers to have winter tires by law, then the case is not safety. 

Hope this helps!

Galina

_3.1. The Lessee shall at any time have the right to purchase the Vehicle(s) from the Lessor at a price which is equal to the agreed residual value of the Vehicle(s) and the VAT according to the legislation in force. If the Lessee wishes to exercise the right to purchase the Vehicle(s) from the Lessor, then the Lessee will inform the Lessor about this_ *_1 month_* _before the expiry of the term of the respective leasing agreement. For the sake of clarity, the Parties confirm that the mentioned notice is not a condition for the Lessee to purchase the Vehicle(s) and the Lessee has the right to purchase the Vehicle(s) from the Lessor at any time regardless of the notice term._ {{The Lessee shall inform the Re-purchaser of its intention to purchase the Vehicle(s). If the Re-purchaser expresses interest in repurchasing the Vehicle(s), the Lessee and the Re-purchaser shall engage in good faith negotiations and attempt to reach an agreement to enable such repurchase. *Update 22.11:*

* Had a discussion with [~accountid:634fb94676b91b62562bc50a] on the possible model design for Assembled
** We will have two sub-models that will be joined into a final one: activity model (agent activity/scheduled activity/conformance/adherence) and event model (agent scheduled events like queue, special leaves etc.)
** Code for both models below
** Dummy design for the model to be done in Google Sheets
** More digging to be done on the events model since we need to slice existing intervals in hour-sized chunks to be able to join with the activity model. 
** Code for activity model:

{noformat}with base as (
    select
        p.email,
        from_unixtime(hr.start_time) AS hour_start,
        from_unixtime(hr.end_time) AS hour_end,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'scheduled_seconds_total' THEN hr.value END) AS seconds_scheduled_total,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'actual_seconds_worked' THEN hr.value END) AS seconds_worked,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'scheduled_seconds_productive' THEN hr.value END) AS seconds_scheduled_productive,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'actual_all_seconds_worked' THEN hr.value END) AS seconds_worked_all,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'actual_utilization' THEN hr.value END) AS utilization_actual,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'schedule_adherence_percentage' THEN hr.value END) AS schedule_adherence_percentage,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'scheduled_seconds_bpo' THEN hr.value END) AS seconds_scheduled_bpo,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'utilization' THEN hr.value END) AS utilization_planned,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'conformance_percentage' THEN hr.value END) AS conformance,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'adherence_percentage' THEN hr.value END) AS adherence_percentage,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'actual_utilization_all_channels' THEN hr.value END) AS utilization_actual_all,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'in_office_shrinkage' THEN hr.value END) AS in_office_shrinkage,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'seconds_in_adherence' THEN hr.value END) AS seconds_in_adherence,
        MAX(CASE WHEN hr.name = 'actual_seconds_in_adherence_bpo' THEN hr.value END) AS seconds_in_adherence_actual_bpo
    from ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.hourly_report_metric hr
    join ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.people p
        on hr.agent_id = p.agent_id
    where hr.type = 'interval'
    group by p.email, from_unixtime(hr.start_time), from_unixtime(hr.end_time)
)


select * from base{noformat}

* Preliminary code for events model (to be modified further to make it joinable with the activity model)

{noformat}SELECT
    at.name,
    p.email,
    from_unixtime(a.start_time) AS start_time,
    from_unixtime(a.updated_at) AS updated_at,
    from_unixtime(a.end_time) AS end_time,
    from_unixtime(a.created_at) AS created_at,
    date_diff('second', from_unixtime(a.start_time), from_unixtime(a.end_time)) AS duration_seconds,
    a.description 
FROM ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.activity a
JOIN ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.activity_type at ON a.activity_type_id = at.id
JOIN ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.people p ON a.agent_id = p.agent_id 
WHERE email = 'joseph.kijana@bolt-outsource.eu' 
     AND a.start_time >= to_unixtime(date_parse('2024-10-18', '%Y-%m-%d'))
    AND a.end_time < to_unixtime(date_parse('2024-10-19', '%Y-%m-%d'))
order by from_unixtime(a.start_time){noformat}

Best to reach out e.g. to Harry Grabham, Lukas Kulertas or Afonso Freitas e Costa to understand how they have worked their magic on this topic with customers but what I see from my end it has often come down to explaining the procedures we have in place to ensure drivers comply with our platform T&Cs, the applicable safety features, and how driver insurance responds to any possible claims. If indeed no luck then I suggest to escalate to Nick to see whether and how far he would be willing to sponsor changing the current practice. ! Draft material for inspiration - subject to modification to meet the market/deal specifics before sharing externally !

Explanation example

_To begin with, Bolt provides ride-hailing services, but it's crucial to understand that we don't own the vehicles, nor do we employ the drivers. This makes it challenging for us to purchase traditional insurance for these vehicles and their activities, due to complexities in demonstrating we have a true insurable interest. While we can opt for a contingent motor liability policy, the effectiveness of such coverage is significantly impacted by the 4th EU Motoring Directive._

_Under the 4th EU Motoring Directive, all EU member states are required to have an uninsured driver protection scheme. This directive mandates that each vehicle must be insured by its owner, making any contingent motor policy we purchase irrelevant. This is because, in many cases, our policy would be secondary to the primary insurance held by the vehicle owner or driver. Additionally, our contracts with drivers and vehicle owners are structured in a way that aligns with this directive, further complicating the insurance landscape._

_Despite these challenges, we are committed to maintaining a responsible platform and ensuring the safety of our passengers. Which includes, but is not limited to:_
_A thorough onboarding process for drivers, which includes checking licences, vehicle eligibility, and insurance coverage for ride-hailing activities._
_Providing safety advisories for drivers and passengers._
_Using services like Onfido for identity verification._
_Continuous validation of documents, with regular audits by us and local authorities._

_Regarding our insurance policies. Bolt's parent company in Estonia and our various country entities purchase their General/Civil Liability insurance individually, which protects our business against potential damages or injuries we might cause._

_It's important to note that these policies do not extend to drivers or vehicles on our platform, as they are not our direct employees or assets. Therefore, they might not be directly relevant to the concerns of a Bolt Ride passenger._

*Legal's recommendation is to wait until after the remaining court hearings to proceed* (likely until end of 2025), *though this ultimately remains a business decision*.*Our reasoning is as follows:*

* *Risk of Backlash:* There is a potential risk of negative reactions due to decreased earnings specially for short-distance trips. This is particularly sensitive given that earnings have been a longstanding issue, as previously highlighted by the government when it introduced the presumption of employment for platform workers in PT.
* *Reclassification Impact:* From a pure reclassification perspective, this change is unlikely to affect the overall strategy, as it does not directly impact operations.

*_Regarding remuneration, our legal position is clear:_*

* _Bolt does not determine the amount couriers are paid._
* _Bolt is unaware of whether couriers receive payments for deliveries or the terms of any such payments._
* _Bolt does not pay couriers directly; payments are made only to fleets._
* _Payments to fleets include amounts received from customers on behalf of the fleet for transport services and settlements for promotional campaigns._
* _Bolt does not know how much couriers earn or whether they negotiate their earnings with the fleet; Bolt is only aware of amounts paid to fleets._

*However, implementing this change now could potentially provide more grounds for certain judges to rule against Bolt, especially if media backlash occurs*. Public perception and media narratives can influence judges, who may form opinions based on news coverage.

Any communication on this matter should only be done to fleets in case the business decision is to move ahead. We are happy to review the draft.

Thank you.

There are two main suspected sources of inaccuracy:

# Rules that affect enrollment but are not included in the model: “treatment_id” from eater test rules, “city_campaign_bypass_signal” from campaign rules etc.
# Overlaps between simultaneously active campaigns, where ones with lower priority (discount) are simply not shown to the user.

I will try to predict the campaign cost estimation error (y) using these features (X) in order to understand their importance.

Other concerns:

* Data reliability – can be solved with backtesting, but it’s setup will take extra time (~ 1 full day).
** Current data consists only of campaigns that got estimated, which is a small percentage. Larger sample might reveal different info.
** Values stored in {{spend_target}} fields in the DB might not be the model’s predictions, but instead human inputs – the fields in admin panel are not write-protected.
** According to Alquamah, campaign setups might change after the cost calculation. The most common case could be post hoc change of {{min_order_value}}.
* Model calculates and returns {{spend_target_absolute}} in EUR, but front-end expects to receive local currency values and therefore displays them with wrong currency prefix. I keep it in mind to fix in the new model service.

Hey [~accountid:712020:13033e65-435c-4794-a380-e007eba7615a] 

Summary of the investigation:
1. Rider reported improper behaviour right after the order was cancelled (24.09.2023 21:56 UK time). 

* Rider advised that the Driver wanted the Rider to cancel the in-app order and to pay for the services with cash.
* Rider report ticket - [*BH1*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/273222108]*.*

2. Later the case was picked up by the Safety team and at 25.09.23, 05:01 UK time, an outbound message was sent to the Driver, requesting their side of events.

* Excerpt from the message: 
_We are reaching out to you from Bolt Customer Safety in regards to a trip you accepted on the 23rd of September at 21:30 from South Terminal, London Gatwick Airport._
_We have received a concerning report from the passenger stating that you kept asking the passenger to cancel the trip and pay you in cash . Bolt takes this type of report seriously, so we have decided to start an investigation._
_Could you kindly elaborate on what happened during this trip and why would we receive a report like this? Please address the allegation._
_Kindly note that we have temporarily suspended your account due to safety concerns. Please provide us with your version of the story._
* In this message, the trip date was written incorrectly - agent stated *23rd* of September, when the trip had occurred on *24th* of September.
* Outgoing message ticket - [*BH2*|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/273278533]

3. 25.09.23, 5:02 UK time - Driver’s account was blocked with an investigative block.

4. 25.09.23, 6:15 UK time - Driver responded, claiming that they didn’t work at all on the 23rd of September and that he must’ve been confused with another Driver.

5. The Safety case was closed at 25.09.23, 6:21 UK time and the account was unblocked 6:29 UK time. Case was closed with status Cannot be Confirmed. 

* Main issue with this investigation is that the Driver was thinking about a different day, therefore they completely dismissed the allegation;
* Agent should’ve realised the mistake and asked for further explanation while referring to the correct date of September 24th;
* Due to this confusion, we do not have a clear understanding of the Driver’s side of events. 
* As it is a High risk type Safety case, the investigative block was placed correctly. As this was the 1st report of offering an off-platform journey, Driver was correctly unblocked and warned. In this case, a correct investigation likely would not have changed the outcome (Driver being unblocked).

Thank you [~accountid:63622ea17d4645af4f03bd18] for pointing out the liability and indemnification clauses.

Indeed, LinkedIn has limited their liability for Personal Data Breaches to their negligence, intentional misconduct, or material failure to comply with the terms of the DPA. In addition, any other failure for LinkedIn to comply with the DPA is capped to the fees paid by Bolt during the term of the applicable Order Forms. This would be 1.3 mln euros under our current Order Form. 

This does diverge from Bolt’s default position which would favor unlimited liability for data protection related infringements or setting 2 mln EUR liability cap. However 1.3 mln EUR in my view is acceptable taking into account the data processing activity in this case. 

Therefore, taking into account the nature of the personal data processed (employee e-mail and activity on the platform), importance of the contract for LinkedIn (trial period offer for complementary licenses) I don’t foresee that we would be successful in negotiating these terms.

ETH came back with their feedback on the DPA, here is the summary:

* They refuse to include *indemnification and liability clauses* in the DPA by misinterpreting the intent and structure of GDPR (see their comment in section 9). Liability clauses in the Research Agreement limit liability to exclude indirect or consequential damages and cap liability for other damages. While this provides a general limitation framework, it does not explicitly include liabilities related to data protection. We cannot sign the DPA which does not offer Bolt proper contractual protections against processor's failures to comply with GDPR.
* Another issue is *data storage*. We usually put data retention periods of 3 months, they propose 10 years. They argue that it is generally accepted worldwide scientific standard to have long storage period for scientific research data only for scientific reasons of reproducibility of research results. We must ensure that the prolonged retention period is justified, well-documented, and proportionate to the research purpose. A vague or blanket justification of "scientific research purposes" may not be sufficient if challenged by a regulator.

I will draft our response to push this topic.

Hey, [~accountid:712020:bb91ac73-536c-48b6-81be-729e20e87df8]. Thank you for your request! 

Let me address your questions one by one:

{quote}For Riders in High and Significant cases, should we provide full refunds to the original payment method of every Rider that opens a CBC or Confirmed High/Significant case? Won’t that make users start accusing Drivers just to get refunds?{quote}

Based on the updated guidelines, if it’s a High/Significant case, we can issue the refund regardless of the outcome of the event. But the most important thing to remember is that when dealing with safety cases, *the highest priority is to solve the user’s issue and ensure they’re safe.* Compensations are a second priority. The main emphasis is on the resolution of the case. Compensation is not a resolution, so it should be issued at the end of the investigation, if applicable. 



{quote}Regarding counterclaims, do I understand correctly that the Rider will only get a refund if they’re the reporting party, as in, if they’re accusing the Driver before they’re accused themselves? Or also in cases when they accuse the Driver after being accused, but before being contacted by us? If it’s the former, doesn’t that mean that if the Rider makes the ticket a few seconds after the Driver or the ticket goes to a different severity they’re more likely to get the refund, meaning it can be up to chance?{quote}

In case of a counterclaim, it would be like this: 

* *No compensation should be issued*
** Rider reported the driver
** CS contacts the driver to investigate
** Driver raises a counterclaim
** Counterclaim against the rider *is confirmed* - no compensation to the rider
* *Compensation should be issued*
** Rider reported the driver
** CS contacts the driver to investigate
** Driver has nothing against the rider, *or* the counterclaim is CBC
** Rider receives a compensation

“If the Rider makes the ticket a few seconds after the Driver…” does not really matter here.  We don’t have to overcomplicate it by thinking about who contacted us first because we're the ones who reach out to the reported party to investigate and seek the applicable solution to the situation. We might not receive a counterclaim straight away, meaning we follow the process and compensate the rider, but the driver can come back at a later time with a counterclaim. This can happen, and there’s no way to predict this. When it comes to safety, we trust the information we have at the time, and we compensate.



{quote}Last but not least, what about cash rides? Should refunds for these be done for cash rides in Safety cases?{quote}

Yes, refunds for cash orders should also be issued. As stated in the Rider guidelines section, you should proceed to the 🐝 [Campaign enrolment via Beehive|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/30729] article. 



If you have any other questions or if something is still unclear, don’t hesitate to let me know in this ticket.  

Wishing you a nice day! 🙂

Seems like specification for the issue label “My drink was spilled” is needed, since it is being used incorrectly:

* Often times, it is actually not clear from the photo that in addition to spilled drink, also the food was damaged. For example, if only a bag from the outside is photographed, it is impossible to say that it wasn’t a bag for drinks solely, but also included some food. Moreover, if a bag without any food items inside is photographed, this should be considered as spilled drink only, not a damaged order. Objectively it seems that refunds for spilled drink + damaged order combined are handed out too easily. In some cases, it is very clear that fries are drowning in drink and in these cases, the combining is justified and correct.
* In case a soup is spilled, it is a damaged order, not a spilled drink.
* Even in cases where clearly only a drink was spilled, damaged order label was also used in combination.



Usage of “My order was damaged” seems to be more clear, as there are examples of hair or other objects being in food and food being damaged (scrambled) due to transportation.

* [XP RH metric groups spreadsheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1wWDrPInawj-Q9eia10KGC85D78iOjF1heRlZO0ATtng/edit?usp=sharing] (RH Metric Groups page).
* [DBT Metrics spreadsheet|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1MMEKS5yY0DCmE4IDHxQCkqK3No4mlySUogyykUaJBi8/edit?usp=sharing].

h3. Key Takeaways

* Our current metrics can be split into *three groups* based on their {{count_expression}}:
** {{green}}: very simple metrics where the aggregators are calculated as {{SUM(metric)}}, {{SUM(POWER(metric), 2)}}, {{COUNT(metric)}}.
** {{yellow}}: simple metrics with the same straightforward sum and square sum definition, but with the count expression being defined as {{COUNT(DISTINCT user_id)}}. We regard this way of defining a metric as an *intended way*. We encourage people to use this metric definition as a template.
** {{red}}: complex metrics where data and count expressions can involve different metrics; for instance, {{avg_user_spend}}. We do not encourage people to create such metrics. However, we still need to support such metrics created so far.
* All metric definitions will live in DBT. These definitions contain only the business logic. No AB Processor parameters have to be defined there.
** The Experimentation team *does not own* the metrics, only uses them.
* All XP metric (aggregator) definitions *reference the dbt metric*.
** For our current {{green}} and {{yellow}} metric groups, we only require to *reference the dbt metric*. For these metric groups, the aggregation type on test/user level is {{SUM}} by default. In case the aggregation type, for some reason, is different, we can define this it in the {{definition.agg}} parameter.
** For our current {{red}} metric group, we require the *reference to dbt metrics* used for both the numerator and denominator. Both these metrics have to have the {{definition.*.metric.agg}} parameter defined.
* MetricFlow is used to generate the query that combines all the necessary dbt metrics for the test.
** This can be a standalone component; it can be a generated dbt model, a separate job, etc.
** We also need to come up with some CI/CD for the new metric addition and data backfilling.
* The user enrollments table is a separate incremental dbt model.
* The resulted MetricFlow query is joined with user enrollments on the randomization unit.
** The query is grouped by the randomization unit, test ID, and test slicers.
** The metrics are thus aggregated using their respective aggregation types ({{SUM}} by default, or the type defined in the {{definition.*.agg}} parameter).
* The *resulted joined query* is then fed to AB Processor along with the *parsed XP aggregator definitions* to then be used for the sum, squared sum, and count expressions calculation.

This approach is validated via the simple PoC implementation. The implementation results are mentioned here: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/XP/boards/525?selectedIssue=XP-2088|https://taxify.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/XP/boards/525?selectedIssue=XP-2088|smart-link].

h2. *Invalid/missing TIN*

The driver is blocked due to an invalid/missing Tax Identification Number (DAC7) and it needs to be updated.

*Current process:*

* In *18* markets drivers can change the TIN number themselves. CS instructs the driver to do it via Driver Portal.
* In the other *4* markets (Austria, Croatia, Germany, Malta), CS escalates the ticket to Local OPS.
* Materials from OPS:
** [+DAC7 local team info page+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PLBK/pages/4656038481/DAC7+local+team+info+page]
** [+Data Validation & Correction Guidelines for ops+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PLBK/pages/4800446922/Data+Validation+Correction+Guidelines+for+ops+WIP]
** [+DAC7 compliance playbook for Local Ops+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PLBK/pages/4231561527/DAC7+compliance+playbook+for+Local+Ops#TIN-codes-in-European-markets]



[+*Data*+|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/support/support_data?qid=s3pQir0xMKOAJUm3tXxv8U&origin=share-slug]:

* *9112* Tier1>Local OPS escalations of blocked driver accounts in the last 6 months.
** Austria - no data
** Croatia - 197
** Germany - 187
** Malta - 227
* The 4 markets cause only *7% of all blocked account escalations* (for all possible reasons). We don’t have separate data of only TIN escalations, this percentage covers all blocked account escalations, thus *TIN escalations are even lower than 7%.*



*How escalation to OPS in the 4 markets could be removed:*

* Agreement with local OPS in Austria, Croatia, Germany and Malta that CS takes over this task from OPS. 
** *Blocker*: due to the importance of the correct TIN number and the compliance risk, it is quite possible that OPS wouldn’t want to give the task to Tier1, thus the Tier1>Tier2 escalation would be needed and it conflicts with the goal of the project.
* The training team would need to create the training for CS about data validation. CS to complete the training.
** *Blocker*: low impact (training only for 4 markets)
* CS needs access to update/validate the TIN in the Admin Panel.
* Process to be created using local OPS playbooks.



*Conclusion:*

* Handling the cases without escalation requires more effort and resources than it does with escalation.
* High compliance risks - cases might need to be handled by Tier2, thus escalation would still exist.
* Low impact - only 4 markets affected and less than 7% of blocked account escalations.

h2. *🇵🇱 Poland* - missing taxicab markings escalations

Only part of OS agents (+ local OPS) are trained to handle these cases due to very high risk from local regulations standpoint.

* (Any) OS agent spots the case and escalates it to the channel
* One of dedicated and trained OS agents picks it up and provides first messages
* If there's proof of the lack of compliance, they escalate it to Local OPS
* Local OPS handle the blocking decision and further communication with the driver
* Local OPS wanted this process to be like this as they're being super careful with compliance issues and they wanted to make the blocking decision themselves. 


Also, these cases have to be handled 24/7 and hence OS (and not IH) take care of them.



h2. *🇿🇦 South Africa* - criminal record check escalations

Process is limited to Tier 2 due to access requirements. The portal used for verifying Criminal Record Checks has a *limited number of accounts permitted*.

OPS team granted permission solely to in-house agents to assist in verifying those documents. In ZA, we get quite a few fake Driver's Licenses, and the available tools to verify the documents are limited. As such, Tier 1 may not be given access or authority to verify PrDPs at this time.

Even though legal does NOT support keeping the clauses as they were, ultimately it will be your decision to make. Please bear in mind though, that in case the risks with it will materialize, the responsibility to deal with the consequences will lay on your team, not legal.

So, what are the risks we might have when keeping it in the original version:

* Firstly, the 50k penalty. As this is an NDA which is a non-transactional document where there is no flow of money, there shouldn’t be limitations on liability. This needs to be evaluated from the perspective of which data are we actually sharing and how much harm would it do to us in case the shared information becomes public. 50k might not cover the costs we actually might face. Having no limitations on liability allows for more comprehensive legal recourse in the event of a breach, enabling the injured party to seek full damages, which could be crucial in case the information is highly sensitive.
* The positive sides of keeping it in a suggested way by legal: no limitations as provided above; only direct and documented damages are claimable. This requirement promotes transparency and makes it more difficult for parties to claim excessive or unfounded damages. By focusing on documented damages, the agreement prioritizes compensation for actual losses incurred, rather than allowing for speculative or punitive damages. 
* Regarding the direct damages vs all damages - by establishing that only direct damages are covered, this can help limit the liability of the disclosing party, preventing claims for indirect, consequential, or punitive damages that could otherwise escalate quickly and lead to significant financial exposure. 

In conclusion, please evaluate what type of information are we sharing and how would it impact us in case it becomes public. 

Please let me know in case you have any further questions!

Hey
Sorry for taking my time to come back here. I have revisited and updated some conventions to make this linking even easier. There are a few different options, I’ll try to add all of them here so we can pick between them. 

*Sample 1 (prio 1)*

Data mart generated from a saved query. 

Example: [mart_city_hour_local_delivery|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:glue,mart_models_spark.mart_city_hour_local_delivery,PROD)/Schema?is_lineage_mode=false&schemaFilter=]

Process: find a saved query, find the corresponding dbt table (will share exactly the same name), read the list of metrics from the saved query metrics section, make the link between the DataHub term (that shares the exact same name with the metric) and the corresponding column in the dbt table (that also has the exact same name). The step of reading the metrics list can also be skipped as we’re pretty confident there are no column that would match a metric name but should not be matched with a term.

*Sample 2*

Data mart defined on top of data marts that are generated from saved queries. Practical use case: mart_city_hour_local (i.e. the equivalent of city kpi) will be a view on top of data marts generated from saved queries. This is lower priority, but ideally we’d still link the terms to the columns of this model as well. No link to share yet, can add here later. 

Process: since we don’t have a saved query, we have a few options. Either we simply rely on a very simple matching of terms to columns in any tables. Or, we add something explicit to initiate this matching for this specific model (e.g. a {{macth_columns_with_terms_in_datahub}} tag on the model). Or, we try to make use of lineage between the tables, for example by checking if lineage exists and columns with the same names exist, then link (this would assume that we do not change column content but keep the same name). 

_If we are going to solve sample 2, we might skip the more rigorous sample 1 solution and go with the more simple sample 2 solution only._ 

*Sample 3 (prio 2)*

Looker view where a measure has been auto-generated from a dbt metric definition

[https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,kpi.view.fact_rides_order_try,PROD)/Schema?is_lineage_mode=false&schemaFilter=rides_cancellation_fees_before_discounts_eur|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,kpi.view.fact_rides_order_try,PROD)/Schema?is_lineage_mode=false&schemaFilter=rides_cancellation_fees_before_discounts_eur]

Process: if the view has been auto-generated (is in the dbt_sync folder) then find all the measures that have a name that matches a term (the name will be an exact match).

NB: The condition of view being auto-generated will prevent us from matching to a view that has not made use of dbt metrics. In reality, false matches will be quite rare, but possible. So here and also in the next two cases the conditions can be there, but as a first iteration it’s also completely fine to not have them. 

*Sample 4*

A Looker view that refines an auto-synced view

Process: TBD. At the moment we don’t have these in DataHub at all? We have built up a carefully choreographed way of syncing to the dbt_sync folder and then always adding a refinement file on top for any additions on Looker side. So this will be a common pattern. The rule could be something like: if the view is a refinement on top of a view that has been auto-generated (is in the dbt_sync folder) then find all the measures that have a name that matches a term (the name will be an exact match).

*Sample 5 (prio 3)*

Looker explore that uses a view that refines an auto-genearted view

[https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,curated.explore.fact_rides_order_try,PROD)/Schema?is_lineage_mode=false&schemaFilter=rides_cancellation_fees_after_discounts_eur_local|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/dataset/urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:looker,curated.explore.fact_rides_order_try,PROD)/Schema?is_lineage_mode=false&schemaFilter=rides_cancellation_fees_after_discounts_eur_local]

Process: Similar to sample 4. If an explore uses an auto-generated view, then match the measures and terms. 

Sample 6

Looker chart that uses measures

[https://datahub.data.boltint.net/chart/urn:li:chart:(looker,dashboard_elements.170391)/Fields?is_lineage_mode=false|https://datahub.data.boltint.net/chart/urn:li:chart:(looker,dashboard_elements.170391)/Fields?is_lineage_mode=false] (probably a bad example as this metric doesn’t have a term because I have defined it with {{create_metric: true}})

Process: TBD. Similar to the above, eventually it uses the measure from a view that has that linking with term.

Hi [~accountid:712020:651f796d-9309-4898-840e-c962fb597c34] !

I have reviewed the contracts and *we can proceed with the project under the terms of existing DPA* but I want to highlight the following risks which differ from Bolt’s general approach to our processors: 

# LinkedIn has limited their liability for Personal Data Breaches to their negligence, intentional misconduct, or material failure to comply with the terms of the DPA. In addition, any other failure for LinkedIn to comply with the DPA is capped to the fees paid by Bolt during the term of the applicable Order Forms. This would be 1.3 mln euros under our current Order Form. 

Bolt’s default position would favor unlimited liability for data protection related infringements or setting 2 mln EUR liability cap. Taking into account the nature of the personal data processed (employee e-mail and activity on the platform), importance of the contract for LinkedIn (trial period offer for complementary licenses) we probably would not be successful in negotiating these terms.

# List of sub-processors is kept online. Therefore Bolt is not explicitly informed of the changes, i.e. Bolt would not give specific written authorization for the appointment of sub-processors.  
# There is no fixed time period for notifying Bolt of receiving data subject right requests, law enforcement requests or SA investigations. It is only stated that “LinkedIN will inform” Bolt about such requests. This might hinder Bolt’s ability to respond to requests in a timely manner.
# Notification of a data breach is set on 48 hours of becoming aware of the data breach. Bolt would ideally require 24hrs generally for the mitigation of risk but we can approve 48hrs.
# Bolt would be responsible for all costs and fees related to Supervisory Authority audit conducted of Bolt in regards to LinkedIn processing activities.
# Upon request LinkedIn will provide a specific audit report conducted by third-party audit firm. For any additional audits Bolt would be responsible for all costs.

Thank you!
Liis

Privacy received a request from [~accountid:712020:92672895-e990-4451-9f97-baec95337272] to assess the lawfulness under Canadian Anti Spam Laws (CASL) of reaching out to dormant drivers in Canada who registered as part of Taxify expansion in 2018 with an update on Hopp launch in 2024/5. # Hard opt-in consent does not expire in Canada - and could be used in 2024.
# Soft opt-in consent is valid in Canada only for 2 years since the last interaction.
# Operational updates such as “Taxify resumes operation in Canada as Hopp” do not require consent under CASL and are not consider promotional.

{noformat}with base as (
	select
		at.name,
		p.email,
		from_unixtime(a.start_time) as start_time,
		from_unixtime(a.updated_at) as updated_at,
		from_unixtime(a.end_time) as end_time,
		from_unixtime(a.created_at) as created_at,
		date_diff('second', from_unixtime(a.start_time), from_unixtime(a.end_time)) as duration_seconds,
		a.description 
	from ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.activity a
	join ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.activity_type at
		on a.activity_type_id = at.id
	join ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.people p
		on a.agent_id = p.agent_id
	where a._fivetran_deleted = false
),
hours as (
    select
        email,
        name,
        created_at,
        updated_at,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        duration_seconds,
        description,
        -- generate the hour-level ranges
        date_trunc('hour', start_time) as hour_start,
        date_trunc('hour', end_time) as hour_end,
        sequence(
            date_trunc('hour', start_time),
            date_trunc('hour', end_time),
            interval '1' hour
        ) as hour_intervals
    from base
),


exploded as (
    select
        email,
        name,
        hour_interval as hour_start,
        date_add('hour', 1, hour_interval) as hour_end,
        start_time,
        end_time,
 		created_at,
        updated_at
    from hours
    cross join unnest(hour_intervals) as t(hour_interval)
)




select * from exploded
where email = 'valentyn.lavrenov@bolt-outsource.eu' and hour_start >= timestamp '2024-11-20' and hour_end < timestamp '2024-11-21'
order by hour_start
limit 100


sliced as (
    select
        email,
        name as event_name,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        least(hour_end, end_time) as least,
        greatest(hour_start, start_time) as greatest,
         least(to_unixtime(hour_end), to_unixtime(end_time)) - 
        greatest(to_unixtime(hour_start), to_unixtime(start_time)) as hourly_duration_seconds,
        start_time,
        end_time
    from exploded
    where hour_start < end_time
),


final as (
	select
		email,
		hour_start,
		hour_end,
		max(case when event_name = 'Queue' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as queue_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Break' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as break_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Day Off' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as day_off_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Social Media' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as social_media_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Other' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as other_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Vacation' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as vacation_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Offline Tasks' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as offline_tasks_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Special Leave' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as special_leave_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Training' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as training_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Price Review' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as pr_duration,
		max(case when event_name = 'Overtime' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as overtime_duration
	from sliced
	where hourly_duration_seconds > 0
	group by email, hour_start, hour_end
)

This is how the logic works (example of a Ride for *10.00 EUR* that is partially covered by a Bolt Business Company coupon of *2.00 EUR*…

Refund logic (i.e. what happens when refund is requested):

* If *refund* requested to *Bolt Balance (BB)*: 
** *8.00 EUR* to *Rider's BB*.
* If *refund* to *original payment method,* e.g. *credit card (CC)*: 
** *8.00 EUR* to *Rider's CC*.
* The *coupon* (or amount expensed to the Business Company for the coupon) *WILL NOT* be refunded in either of the above cases:
** i.e. We *WILL NOT* credit *2.00 EUR* back to the Business Company.
** Once the coupon has been used, it is gone.
* Customer Support/Account Managers can issue a new coupon at their own discretion.

There are two sets of such measures:

*AIRWALLEX TECHNICAL AND ORGANISATIONAL SECURITY MEASURES - measures AWX takes to protect the data*

_Description of the technical and organisational measures implemented by the data importer(s) (including any relevant certifications) to ensure an appropriate level of security, taking into account the nature, scope, context and purpose of the processing, and the risks for the rights and freedoms of natural persons._
Airwallex has implemented an information security management system aligned with ISO27001 and certified as meeting SOC2 Type II, as summarised below:
1: *Information security policies*
Airwallex has implemented security policies and standards that are constantly reviewed in line with the overall direction of the organisation’s information security practices. Risk assessments are performed on a regular basis and agreed mitigating controls are included in the policies, standards and procedures to address security globally.
2: *Organisation of information security*
Airwallex’s information security policies and standard assign responsibilities for information security related tasks. It ensures that the organisation has established a framework that can adequately implement and maintain information security practices within the organisation supported by senior leadership.
3: *Human resource security*
Airwallex ensures individuals are screened before employment, makes sure that employees and contractors understand their responsibilities and addresses their responsibilities when they no longer hold that role – either because they’ve left the organisation or changed positions.
# *Security controls*
Airwallex has implemented a set of information security controls to mitigate risks. These controls are developed through risk assessments and a cybersecurity strategy, and demonstrate commercially reasonable efforts to protect sensitive data stored and processed by Airwallex.

*CUSTOMER (Bolt) TECHNICAL AND ORGANISATIONAL SECURITY MEASURES - measures Bolt must take to protect the data exchanged with AWX:*

_Description of the technical and organisational measures implemented by the data importer(s) (including any relevant certifications) to ensure an appropriate level of security, taking into account the nature, scope, context and purpose of the processing, and the risks for the rights and freedoms of natural persons._

# *Physical Access Control* 
The Customer shall take, among others, the following technical and organizational measures in order to establish the identity of the authorized persons and prevent unauthorized access to the Customer’s premises and facilities in which personal data is processed:
* All entrances are locked and can only be accessed with the appropriate key / chip card
* Windows and doors are protected by an alarm system
* All visitors are required to present identification and are signed in by authorized staff
* Video monitoring of visitors
* Visitors are accompanied by Customer’s personnel at all times
* Full perimeter and interior surveillance cameras
* Use of motion detectors to monitor sensitive areas
* Trained security guards are stationed in and around the building 24x7 
* Co-location facility - separate locked server suites with card readers

# *System Entry Control*  
The Customer shall take, among others, the following technical and organizational measures in order to prevent unauthorized access to the data processing systems:
* Unique user authentication via user name and password for each network and system access required (default passwords changed at 1st login)
* Use of state-of-the-art anti-virus software that includes e-mail filtering and malware detection
* Use of firewalls
* During idle times, user and administrator PCs are automatically locked 
* User passwords are changed at least every 90 days and only allow complex passwords
* Concept of least privilege, allowing only the necessary access for users to accomplish their job function. Access above these least privileges requires appropriate authorization
* Starter, mover & leaver housekeeping processes in place which covers role-based access rights
* IT access privileges are reviewed regularly (at least every quarter) by appropriate personnel
* RSA 2-factor authentication in place for remote connections
* Network monitoring services in place 24 x 7 x 365 to detect unauthorized activities
* Vulnerability scanning and remediation in place
* Data centre and website penetration testing programme in place 

# *Data Access Control*  
The Customer shall take, among others, the following technical and organizational measures in order to prevent unauthorized activities in the data processing systems outside the scope of any granted authorizations:
* User and administrator access to the network is based on a role based access rights model. There is an authorization concept in place that grants access rights to data only on a “need to know” basis
* Administration of user rights through system administrators
* Number of administrators is reduced to the absolute minimum
* IT governance & controls audits undertaken annually by external 3rd party
* Internal control audits undertaken regularly
* Network monitoring services in place 24 x 7 x 365 to detect unauthorized activities

# *Data Transfer Control*
The Customer shall take, among others, the following technical and organizational measures in order to ensure that personal data cannot be read, copied, altered or removed by unauthorized persons under their electronic transmission or during their transport or recording on data carriers and to guarantee that it is possible to examine and establish where personal data are or have had to be transmitted by data transmission equipment:
* Remote access (including during remote maintenance or service procedures) to the IT systems only via VPN tunnels or other state-of-the-art secure, encrypted connections
* Use of e-mail encryption
* Data transferred by the Customer is transported and saved in encrypted form. The relevant areas of the data carriers are encrypted using data and hard drive encryption software
* Data storage devices and paper documents are locked away when not in use (clean desk policy)
* Physical transports are only performed with locked containers and/or guarded vehicles
* Use of document shredders
* Secure destruction processes in place to industry standards utilising specialised 3rd party with disposal certificates produced
* The secure transfer modes and encryption methods are regularly updated and kept state-of-the-art (e.g., according to the recommendations in the data protection manual issued by the BSI (Federal Office for Information Security))
* 3rd party secure off-site tape storage utilised
* Secure communication session established via HTTPS and SFTP protocols across all applications / services
* Encrypted certificates utilised for authentication between the web client and the web server across all websites

# *Input Control* 
The Customer shall take, among others, the following technical and organizational measures in order to ensure that it is subsequently possible to verify and establish whether and by whom personal data have been entered into data processing systems, altered or removed:
Access to electronic documents / applications is documented via auditable log files 
Access to physical documents is documented via protocols 
Protocolling input, modification and deletion of data by use of individual user names

# *Control of Instructions* 
The Customer shall take, among others, the following technical and organizational measures in order to ensure that personal data which are processed on behalf of Data Controller can only be processed in compliance with Data Controller’s instructions:
* Clear and binding internal policies contain formalized instructions for data processing procedures 
* Unambiguous language in the underlying contracts
* Careful selection of contractors, especially with regard to data security aspects
* Internal monitoring of quality of service includes compliance with contractual arrangements
* Regular audits by 3rd parties include compliance with contractual arrangements
* Regular staff training to ensure compliance with contractual arrangements and maintain awareness regarding data protection requirements
* ecure destruction processes in place to industry standards utilising specialised 3rd party with disposal certificates produced
* Periodic risk assessments focus on how insider access is controlled and monitored
* The Customer’s corporate network is separated from its Customer services network by means of complex segregation devices

# *Availability Control* 
The Customer shall take, among others, the following technical and organizational measures in order to protect the data from accidental destruction or loss: 
* Appliances for the monitoring of temperature and humidity 
* Fire / smoke detectors and fire extinguishers in the areas where data is stored / processed
* State of the art firewall
* Use of state-of-the-art anti-virus software that includes e-mail filtering and malware detection
* Data recovery measures and emergency plan in place and regularly tested
* Implementation of state-of-the-art backup methods such as: tape backup, data mirroring, and so on. Physical separation of the backup data. Data stored in the archive is saved using redundant systems.
* Uses a combination of full, differential, and cumulative backups to ensure data integrity and timely restoration 
* Backup tapes are securely stored both on-site and off-site to provide protection against disaster and efficient data recovery
* To ensure an uninterrupted supply of power to the system, redundant power supply units are built into the systems wherever possible. 
* Data is stored redundantly on multiple devices 
* Integrity of stored data regularly verified using checksums
* Automated processes move data traffic away from affected area to uncompromised area in case of failure
* Preventative maintenance is performed to ensure continued operability of equipment

# *Separation and Purpose Control* 
The Customer shall take, among others, the following technical and organizational measures in order to ensure that data collected for different purposes are processed separately:
* Documents that are stored physically are stored separately for each Customer and the respective containers are clearly labelled 
* Implementation of an authorization concept
* Logical separation of electronically stored Customer data (on the software side). Each client has its own designated database for storing information, to ensure that each client’s data is isolated from any other client's data
* Strong isolation between guest virtual machines is maintained. Partners are prevented from accessing areas not assigned to them by filtering through the virtualization software.
* A unique encryption key is created per Customer

The firmware was tested and it “converted” the helmet lock to Cable lock.

* Firmware can be applied to Helmet lock module and cable lock module. Hatch lock reject it
* When helmet lock and cable lock are attached to the scooter at the same time, the cable lock responds to cable lock commands as expected. There were no conflicts between the helmet and Cable lock while locking or unlocking the locks.
* It is possible to actuate helmet and cable lock at the same time.
* There is a delay between initial init of the helmet and cable locks - helmet lock inits first, then cable lock inits.

The testing was done using CAN protocol tester and Kvaser. IoT was not used to upgrade the firmware nor send the commands to the locks.

Firmware is OK to use.

_A Bolt é uma sociedade comercial que tem vindo a cumprir e pretende continuar a cumprir com todas as disposições legais que lhe sejam aplicáveis._ -_Com efeito, a Bolt não tem conhecimento de se encontrar na presente data a infringir com qualquer norma que resulte quer do Regulamento Geral do Ruído, quer do Regulamento de Horários de Funcionamento dos Estabelecimentos de Venda ao Público e de Prestação de Serviços no Concelho de Lisboa. Assim, cumpre notar que o estabelecimento comercial explorado pela Bolt Market está a atuar dentro dos horários de funcionamento legalmente permitidos, podendo inclusivamente estar em pleno funcionamento aos fins de semana, feriados e durante a noite. Em boa verdade, os fornecedores da Bolt Market - que poderiam eventual provocar mais ruído devido ao processo de cargas e descargas  - apenas entregam mercadorias entre as 9h00 e as 19h00 de segunda-feira a sexta-feira_-{color:#006644} -_e a título excecional ao sábado_-{color}-_, o que, salvo melhor opinião, poderá considerar-se com sendo um horário razoável. Ultrapassado esse horário, a Bolt Market não aceita mais entregas de mercadorias. Já os pedidos que são entregues aos estafetas poderão igualmente ocorrer durante o período da noite. Sucede que ajustar este último horário é totalmente incomportável para o bom funcionamento da atividade comercial da Bolt Market na medida em que é precisamente esse o período durante o qual são recebidos mais pedidos de compra._- _No entanto, novamente numa lógica de boa-fé, a Bolt Market irá tentar reduzir ao máximo o eventual ruído que resulte das entregas com os fornecedores. Para além deste esforço, e já no que diz respeito à entrega de mercadorias pelo fornecedores, a Bolt Market irá solicitar aos fornecedores que vêm entregar mercadorias logo pela manhã que desliguem os seus veículos aquando das entregas para reduzir o ruído na via pública. Contudo, uma vez mais, dado que os aludidos fornecedores não são trabalhadores da Bolt Market, tal poderá não surtir o efeito pretendido e a recomendação poderá não ser acatada._ 

# *Ruído Excessivo e Contínuo*

_A Bolt Market dedica a sua atividade comercial ao funcionamento de um mercado/mercearia online de produtos alimentares, sendo certo que o estabelecimento comercial em causa gere os pedidos de produtos que são solicitados pelos utilizadores da plataforma, organiza-os, entrega aos estafetas que vêm recolhê-los ao estabelecimento, e também aceita entregas de mercadorias de fornecedores. Em suma, a atividade que_ -_alegadamente_- _produz um ruído excessivo e contínuo diz respeito apenas e tão-só ao processo de entrega e recolha de produtos alimentares. A Bolt Market acredita que,_ -_é de senso comum_- _que esta concreta atividade não produz o mesmo ruído que seja suscetível de provocar a diminuição da qualidade de vida dos moradores, quando comparando com outro tipo de atividades comerciais que se registam na cidade de Lisboa._

_Acresce que, a Bolt Market, por ser, como se disse, um mercado/mercearia online de produtos alimentares, necessita encarecidamente de utilizar sistemas de ar condicionado e que estes estejam em pleno funcionamento para conseguir garantir as normas de Qualidade e Segurança Alimentar. Neste sentido, é manifestamente impossível retirar os sistemas de ar condicionado por estes serem imprescindíveis não só para o pleno funcionamento da atividade comercial da Bolt Market, mas também para que a Bolt Market cumpra com todas as normas de higiene alimentar e de saúde relativamente às quais está legalmente obrigada. No entanto, damos nota de que relativamente a este tema, será em breve (ou eventualmente já terá sido) contactado, na qualidade de advogado mandatado pelo condomínio porquanto o proprietário do local no qual a Bolt Market exerce a sua atividade contratou um técnico de sistemas de ar condicionado para verificar se existe alguma possibilidade de reduzir o ruído produzido pelos mesmos._

_Conforme pode constatar, a Bolt Market encontra-se comprometida a zelar pelo bem-estar dos moradores em causa, pretendendo em total boa-fé implementar todas as soluções que permitam mitigar quaisquer danos decorrentes da sua atividade, em adequada proporção com a necessidade de manter a sua atividade comercial em pleno funcionamento, dentro dos moldes expectáveis e aceitáveis._

_A Bolt Market mantém-se igualmente disponível para dialogar, caso considere necessário._

_Com os melhores cumprimentos,_

+*ANALYSIS*+

* *Deadline*: Not specified, but ASAP
* *Requestor*: Coventry City Council (Licensing Enforcement Officer)
* *Request*: Driver order history for specific times.
** “_Confirm driver records for time between 1230-1330hrs Saturday 5th October 2024 and 1430-1530hrs Wednesday 30th October 2024 for UBER private hire vehicle black coloured BMW 520d bearing registration number AF63UHO and for which Local Authority it is licensed_”
** It is odd that the driver is stated as driving for Uber. However, council has insisted that he works for Bolt (as well as Uber). Authority just wants confirmation that he was working on the Bolt app during the stated periods and not displaying licence, so that authority can piece the picture together.
** Safety Team has confirmed that driver was not driving during the stated periods.
* *Context*: Information needed to investigate failure to display PHV licence plate on the dates specified, contrary to Section 48(6) Local Government (Misc Provisions) Act 1976. Prosecution being sought.
* *Validity*: Confirmed
** Looks official. Signed and dated.
* *Legal* *Basis*: Authority has not been helpful here, but IMO we have enough.
** Originally, legal basis cited as Schedule 2 Part 1(2) DPA (information necessary for prevention / detection of crime and apprehension of offenders).
*** This provisions exempts DSSR requirements etc., but not lawfulness requirement. As such, lawful basis still needed to disclose.
** Authority then responded citing various different legal provisions and a threat.
*** Town Police Clauses Act 1847 / Local Government (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1976 / Transport Act 1985 / Equality Act 2010 / Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994 - Not helpful. No specific provisions cited.
*** PACE 1984 - Again, not helpful. No specific provisions cited.
*** Section 48(6) LGMPA 1976 - Not helpful. Sets out offences, not power of authority to request information.
*** Section 73(1) LGMPA 1976 - This is arguably the most helpful citation. Offence to fail to give an authorised officer (the requestor appears to be one) any info they may reasonably require for the performance of their function.
** IMO, we can generally rely on legitimate interests in disclosing this info.
*** Not ideal, but given that the data is extremely limited and non-sensitive, and given that it concerns the prosecution of an offence, the harms resulting from not disclosing it are greater than disclosing it.
*** As I side note, I also get the sense that the requestor is not very clued-in on the relevant legal provisions here. I doubt that asking for a more specific legal basis is going to bear any fruit.
* *Proportionality*: Confirmed
** Effectively saying that a driver was not driving for Bolt during those periods if very low risk. It also makes sense why the authority is asking for this.
* *Comments* / *Next* *Steps*:
** Ask Alfred to confirm that we are 100% sure that the driver did not take trips during the specified periods. If so, this information is very low risk for us to provide, and is not worth the obstruction.
*** We do not want to risk breaching any licence conditions here. IMO, on balance, we should provide the confirmation and close this out.

I had a discussion with [@piotr.rzasa|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U043YSVBVAL], who is working on creating the history management table for T3 cities. We explored two possible approaches for structuring the table, outlined below:
*Case 1:*

{noformat}01-01-2025, group A, city 123, ADDED  
04-01-2025, group A, city 123, REMOVED

{noformat}01-01-2025, group A, [123, 124, 125]  
04-01-2025, group A, [124, 125]  
08-01-2025, group A, [123, 124, 125]  
09-02-2025, group A, [123, 124, 125, 126, 127]  {noformat}

In this approach, the table would record the entire state of the city group if there is any change in the group. Initially, the current city group structure would be captured, and subsequent changes (additions/removals) would update the state with new row in history table. *Update 26.11:* 

* Latest query: 

{noformat}-- Step 1: Base data extraction
with base as (
    select
        at.name as event_name,
        p.email,
        from_unixtime(a.start_time) as start_time,
        from_unixtime(a.updated_at) as updated_at,
        from_unixtime(a.end_time) as end_time,
        from_unixtime(a.created_at) as created_at,
        date_diff('second', from_unixtime(a.start_time), from_unixtime(a.end_time)) as duration_seconds,
        a.description
    from ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.activity a
    join ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.activity_type at
        on a.activity_type_id = at.id
    join ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.people p
        on a.agent_id = p.agent_id
    where a._fivetran_deleted = false
),


-- Step 2: Generate hour-level ranges
hours as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        created_at,
        updated_at,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        duration_seconds,
        description,
        date_trunc('hour', start_time) as hour_start,
        date_trunc('hour', end_time) as hour_end,
        sequence(
            date_trunc('hour', start_time),
            date_trunc('hour', end_time),
            interval '1' hour
        ) as hour_intervals
    from base
),


-- Step 3: Explode hourly intervals
exploded as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        hour_interval as hour_start,
        date_add('hour', 1, hour_interval) as hour_end,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        created_at,
        updated_at
    from hours
    cross join unnest(hour_intervals) as t(hour_interval)
),


-- Step 4: Slice events to fit within hourly intervals
sliced as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        least(hour_end, end_time) as least_end_time,
        greatest(hour_start, start_time) as greatest_start_time,
        least(to_unixtime(hour_end), to_unixtime(end_time)) - 
        greatest(to_unixtime(hour_start), to_unixtime(start_time)) as hourly_duration_seconds,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        updated_at
    from exploded
    where hour_start < end_time
),


-- Step 5: Detect overlapping events within the same hour
overlaps_resolved as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        hourly_duration_seconds,
        updated_at,
        row_number() over (
            partition by email, event_name, hour_start, hour_end 
            order by updated_at desc 
        ) as row_num,
        -- Detect if the events overlap with any other event within the same hour
        case 
            when exists (
                select 1
                from sliced s2
                where s2.email = sliced.email
                and s2.hour_start = sliced.hour_start
                and s2.hour_end = sliced.hour_end
                and s2.start_time < sliced.end_time
                and s2.end_time > sliced.start_time
                and s2.updated_at != sliced.updated_at
            ) then 1
            else 0
        end as is_overlapping
    from sliced
),


-- Step 6: Filter out duplicates and non-overlapping events
filtered as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        hourly_duration_seconds,
        updated_at
    from overlaps_resolved
    where (is_overlapping = 0 or row_num = 1)
),


-- Step 7: Aggregate durations by event type
final as (
    select
        email,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Queue' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as queue_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Break' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as break_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Day Off' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as day_off_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Social Media' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as social_media_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Other' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as other_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Vacation' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as vacation_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Offline Tasks' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as offline_tasks_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Special Leave' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as special_leave_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Training' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as training_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Price Review' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as pr_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Overtime' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as overtime_duration
    from filtered
    group by email, hour_start, hour_end
)


-- Step 8: Output the results
select * from final
limit 100;{noformat}

* Issues: definition of is_overlapping is not entirely correct. Logic needs to be refined considering all possible cases when overlap of events happens

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

* *Order History*

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;

* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights*

Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

I think this may require major resource to map out and develop, in which case you'd need to business case it and put it on the MVRA roadmap etc. You're best off discussing these proposals with [~accountid:712020:209f6e12-e421-4fbf-9a9f-60d100117bab] [~accountid:61fd40abc224b80069c9d6cf] and [~accountid:5e2af09cc55f580c9fca70a7] at first instance, but here's some key thoughts:

* The local legal team (working with reg.) would need to identify the suitable 'aggregator co', navigating through licensing issues of who has the right to use the technology. 
* If the operator is not Bolt, then really the terms and conditions (and operational management) shouldn't belong to Bolt either - if we want to keep the operations segregated for reclassification purposes; so we'd need to identify what sort of T+C approval processes we'd want in place. If in reality we retain control over the terms between fleets and riders, then I think the fleet will be considered to be subordinate to Bolt. 
* Product development work will be needed to execute any necessities re: the above^^^.
* We'd need to navigate this issue with licensing authorities - that's one for [~accountid:5e2af09cc55f580c9fca70a7]'s team.
* Have a look on [this|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1BS2c0Yptc_FLCJwmkz6btbpZT0GhQFR2czaSqAUwhHg/edit?tab=t.0] note on reclassification + fleets generally. In short, we shouldn't expect to be able to impose controls on fleets that have the effect (in reality) of imposing controls over drivers without creating consequences for the fleet and for Bolt. Granted, there is more scope to do this outside of the EU (and outside the remit of the Platform Work Directive). 
* Any controls should be as per that note: ideally, nothing should impose controls over specific drivers / vehicles, but the fleet as a whole. 
* If Bolt is primarily trying to offload liability by using the fleet as a proxy, a well-advised fleet in the UK (noting the Uber and Bolt litigation) might be very wary of imposing controls over drivers, if it doesn't employ them.

*** Explain how rider ratings are calculated, that we currently do not block riders for a low rating / Bolt does not take take any corrective / punitive measures against riders (such as blocking) for bad ratings.
*** Explain that we cannot delete / correct ratings on the grounds of inaccuracy. Ratings and feedback are inherently subjective, reflecting personal experiences and perceptions rather than factual data, and this subjectivity is unavoidable.
*** Explain that allowing drivers and riders to express opinions promotes a safer platform, as feedback can help highlight behaviours that may compromise safety, even if perceptions differ between parties.
*** As a mitigation effort, we can reiterate to the rider that they can request a copy of their data, or delete their account.

Dear Jan,

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 2 November 2024.

Unfortunately, we are unable to action your request for the following reasons:

* Your average rating is calculated based on the ratings provided by drivers over the previous 365-day period. Each of these ratings provided by drivers are inherently and unavoidably subjective, reflecting the personal experiences and perceptions of individual drivers rather than factual information. As such, these ratings cannot be corrected on the grounds of inaccuracy.
* Bolt allows drivers to express opinions about riders through ratings to provide additional reassurance to drivers and to provide a safe and accountable marketplace environment. This in turn empowers drivers to make informed decisions about accepting or declining ride requests and exercise greater control over their working environment. It is therefore of utmost importance that these ratings are maintained on our platform in accordance with applicable laws.

For more information about how Bolt processes your personal data in this regard, we refer you to our privacy notice available at [https://bolt.eu/es-es/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides|https://bolt.eu/es-es/privacy/privacy-for-riders/?category=rides]. 

In any event, please note the following:

* Bolt will not take any corrective or punitive measures against riders for a low rating. Any suspensions applied to a rider’s account in connection with their rider rating will only limit the rider’s ability to order a ride, and will not limit their access to the rest of the Bolt App, or to any other of our services.
* As noted in previous messages, you can request access to your personal data and/or request the deletion of your Bolt account at any time.

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You have the right to complain directly to the appropriate supervisory authority and seek a judicial remedy. If you have any additional questions, please let us know.

Yours sincerely,

*Bolt Privacy Team*

When defining the communication standards with your Leads for Business, we focused on maintaining professionalism while adhering to a *business communication style.*

So, we have three scenarios with the user’s comm:

# *First email/message*: Name always included
# *Followup reply*: Name might be omitted if the reply is within an hour
# *After a break (>1 hour)*: Name always included

I understand your point about the second scenario, and I agree that within an hour, there’s no strict need to repeat the name. However, it’s important to have *clear* and defined guidelines to avoid confusion for agents and ensure we maintain *high objectivity in the review process*.

Regarding the data and deep dive, I’d like to point out that a 50-ticket sample mixing different verticals doesn’t provide much insight. I checked 500 cases in [Looker|https://bolt.cloud.looker.com/explore/support/support_data?qid=jMKebqhFWSINHu8yyensGB&toggle=fil], which shows:

* Only *37.5%* of follow-up replies are sent within an hour (including closings and escalations ❗ )
* The *average response time* for follow-up replies is over *2,800 minutes* (~2 days).
* The *median response time* is *171 minutes*, which is almost 3 hours.

Considering this, I believe the proposed change is not impactful enough to justify implementing the "within an hour" rule. Using the user’s name doesn't affect communication standards and it would increase the time for reviewers to check times.

Hey [~accountid:63abfbea7cde7bff9d78a2af] ! Thanks a lot for checking the issue. I have a few comments about this: 

1. “_therefore agents should not provide a compensation for the second time” -_ For a lot of use cases, there are no rules in the KB article stating that compensation cannot be issued if the case is repetitive. For example, GPS issues. We have this KB article: 🛴 [Scooter/e-bike rider: I was charged more than expected|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360008601894] and 🛴 [Micromobility compensation guidelines|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/8602030908178]. In both, we only have this, with no mention that compensation cannot be issued if it is the second time: 

* _If you confirm a GPS issue that resulted in an overcharge, refund 50% of the trip fare to the user's Bolt Balance. See 🛴 Micromobility compensation guidelines_
* _If the user insists on a full refund, proceed with issuing a full refund in Admin Panel (you'll have the option even if you've already issued a partial refund)_ 

For all other cases (issues with brakes, tyres, battery, etc), where the vehicle is faulty, we only have this mentioned: 

•*Service not provided; less than 100m covered:* Refund 100% of the trip price
•*Service provided; more than 100m covered:* Refund 50% of the trip price

That’s why the issue appeared, as I described above: the user contacted us 3 times regarding the problems with the scooter/orders, and the agents wrongly determined that these were GPS issues. No rule implies restrictions on the amount of compensation for this type of issue. As there were no restrictions on the time frame in which such compensations could be provided either.

2. _“We should not restrict compensation unless the requests are repetitive and appear to be fraudulent” -_ while it is absolutely clear to us, we have noticed that OS agents usually do not step out from the KB and strictly follow the rules described there. They don't always take a common-sense approach, which is why they prefer to issue a refund rather than investigate further. It would be helpful to provide them with recommendations, such as checking the user’s comments, recent cases, and the number of refunds issued recently, and so on. It may sound simple, however, it would be beneficial to have it written in the KB for OS agents. 

3. *Why are we raising this topic?* We’ve been approached by the Fraud team regarding fraud incidents in Germany. Here is what they said: 

_We have finished investigating the issue and, the main issue is in Germany, with USA cards but of course we have other markets. Refunds that happened more than 30 days after order creation. 19% of the total refunds match this condition._

* _We can not confirm that all of them are fraud, but we are investigating._

* _Refunds that happened more than 30 days after order creation with USA cards and the user had a small fraud flag._ *_10% of the total refunds match these conditions._*
** _We can confirm that most of them are fraud._
** _Some of the orders even have a chargeback, meaning they were stolen cards. Fraud is loosing triple the money._
*** _Money is taken away from our app._
*** _Money is being refunded to the fraudster's balance._
*** _With possitive balance the user gets a type of "inmmunity" and starts again doing more fraud._

[_@mari.hiie_|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U07EV77L6HG] _is going to work manually blacklist/block the most fraudulent users to reduce this from further escalating. But we need more help from CS._
_Soon the country manager will wonder why there is a extra lost on DE metrics._

So, 10% of the fraudulent refunds is significant. 175 users have already been blocked, but this may not be the end.

With that being said, we can definitely provide feedback to the suppliers, but this would be more effective if rules were clearly stated in the KB articles and compensation guidelines. Based on the above, it would be especially helpful to have rules that specify restrictions on compensation for repetitive cases, as well as guidelines for additional checking and investigation.
