Hi [~accountid:712020:0f7a089b-3b06-423b-844c-6e5ac370aa1e] - apologies for the delay. I have now reviewed and my comments are as follows:

# I have included one final round of comments in [this document|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NU8UKWLXrNllCaHqURc6dwzHVNPuWSkv/edit#bookmark=id.35nkun2]. Please put these amendments to Zoom.
# Assuming that Zoom will again reject all of these comments, then we will not propose any more from the Privacy side. This does not block Bolt from signing the agreement, but the business should be aware of the risks that it will be accepting in this case.

I include more detail on each of these two points below.

*1. Final round of comments*

* Zoom has refused all of our suggested amendments to the DPA, on the grounds that Zoom does not as standard make changes to its DPA on a per-customer basis. This is not especially surprising given that kind of organisation that Zoom is.
* Ultimately, in most instances we can live with no changes being made to Zoom’s DPA. This is particularly the case due to the risk profile being relatively low, in light of the majority of data  processed under this agreement being low-risk.
* However, there are certain items (particularly with regards to indemnities) that would expose Bolt to significant risk if not addressed (see further details in Section 2 below). As such, it is worth pushing one more time solely for these items, just in case there is a chance that Zoom will accept them in a more stripped-back form.
* I have therefore included one final round of minimal edits to the DPA in [this document|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NU8UKWLXrNllCaHqURc6dwzHVNPuWSkv/edit#bookmark=id.35nkun2]. Please put these amendments to the Zoom team, and explain that we have set out our reasoning as comments in the document.

*2. Risk of accepting the DPA with no amendments*

* If Zoom does not accept these amendments (my prediction is they will not), then we will not propose anything further from the Privacy side. This does not necessarily act as a blocker to signing the agreement as a whole.
* However, when making its final decision, the business should be aware that by accepting the DPA without any of Privacy’s amendments, it would be accepting the following risks should something ‘go wrong’.
* For example, let’s say that Zoom suffered a personal data breach that affected Bolt customer data, and we discovered that Bolt needed to notify the data protection regulators about this:
** *Delayed notification / fines*: In this example, Bolt would need to notify the regulators within a specified timeframe. However, the unamended DPA does not set a specific deadline by which Zoom should provide Bolt with all the necessary information to do so. This means that Bolt may not be able to notify the regulators in time, which could damage our relationship with them. In such circumstances, the regulators could also order corrective action and/or fines against Bolt.
** *Difficult recovery*: The unamended DPA does not include pro-Bolt indemnities for any data protection non-compliance by Zoom. Referring again to the above example, if the data breach was Zoom’s fault and Bolt was fined by a regulator as a result of this, it would be difficult for Bolt to recover the fine amount from Zoom. Also, given the liability cap of 240k in the main agreement, even if Bolt could recover some money from Zoom, this may not be sufficient to cover Bolt’s total liability (as a data protection regulator could fine Bolt up to EUR 20m / 4% of worldwide turnover).
** *Increased risk of non-cooperation / costs of investigation*: If Bolt then wanted to ensure that this kind of incident did not happen again, under the unamended DPA Bolt would have to bear the costs of investigating Zoom’s data protection compliance and making recommendations. This would result in further financial liability on Bolt’s side.
* Please note that the above is a snapshot of the risks that Bolt could be exposed to by accepting the unamended DPA. The core amendment that we are pushing for here is the pro-Bolt indemnity / removal of the 240k liability cap, for the reasons we have set out previously on this SD ticket. This is the main risk that the business needs to be aware of.
* If the business is ok with these risks, then it can proceed with signing the agreement without any of our proposed changes to the DPA.

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* which you are entitled. This includes:

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

Hi Asnate!

I think this was covered through the in-house team and hopefully the answer got to you already. However, just in case, with a terrible delay for which I apologise, I will also add it here:

We will probably need to add some specification to the article to make this clear.

However, it's all about the details - phrasing and timing.

As we keep repeating (too much maybe), the blocks are here to allow for contextual support and context is what you need to determine what's okay and what brings no value. Let's break it up a bit:

Scenario 1: First agent interaction

* When a customer contacts us and reaches the first agent then saying stuff like "I am here to help" or "I will be happy to help" or "I will gladly assist you" really doesn't bring much value because well, that's their job
* It's much better to just say "Hey, I'm Michaela from the Bolt Support Team!" and get on with the solution.

Scenario 2: Ongoing conversation

* The customer's issue is still not getting resolved and they've already spoken to 3 different agents and you come in - the customer doesn't need to know that you are from Bolt or the Support Team anymore, they already heard that
* It doesn't sound natural in this scenario if every new agent says "Hey, I'm Michaela from Bolt". Just saying "Hey, this is Michaela" sounds a bit rude
* In this case you need to offer some kind of transition for the customer as you are letting him know that yet another person came to try to resolve their request
* For this scenario, it's completely okay to say "I'll be helping from here" because it means "I will take over and help now [because my colleagues before me didn't/couldn't do that for whatever reason]"

I am sure it's clear that there is a difference between the meaning of "Hey, you've reached customer support and I am a customer support agent and will be helping you" vs "Hey, sorry it's taking forever and I'm like the third person on here, but I will take over your case now and try to help" (we can't say it quite so blatantly but the context is implied and maybe we just need to make sure this is clear in the examples shared in the documentation)

I hope this helps 🌻

Additionally, when issue keys become too granular, our issue prediction model struggles to differentiate between them, often assigning a 50% probability to both. This leads to indecision and can ultimately lower the automation rate.

Adding or modifying issue keys should only be allowed if other configs don’t rely on them and if the keys are correct. Another issue we’ve noticed is the reuse of issue keys - sometimes an existing key is renamed (only the title, not the actual key), instead of adding a new one.

Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 



We share the copy of all recorded locations of your use of the Bolt App in the attached file. This includes:



* Location data of your micromobility orders and routes.





*Answer to question 2*



Bolt collects data about your precise and/or approximate geolocation (including GPS, and IP address) from your mobile device when you open and continue using the Bolt App during the active order. We also track the precise location of e-scooters and e-bikes at all times that includes the duration of the customer’s orders and the location of nearby e-scooters and e-bikes to you when you open the Bolt App. When the order is placed by you in the Bolt App,  we collect the address when your order is started, the date and time of an order, geolocation of an e-scooter or e-bike during the order and the final destination of your order. *Answer to question 3*



Apple or Google enables apps to automatically trigger notifications when the user enters a specific geographical area. This does not require the app to run in background and mobile data to be used. Apple or Google stores this information and automatically triggers those notifications without sharing the user’s location with Bolt. 



You can read more about the functionality directly on Apple’s website[ here|https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/unlocationnotificationtrigger].

The current implementation of the deploy-only release pipeline in the Builder has some limitations:

* It is possible to release only whole packages. Selecting specific services from a package is not possible. Because of this limitation, it is not possible to apply changes to a specific service/services from a package. Supporting service-specific deploy-only pipelines might be challenging as it requires changes that affect a lot of places: pipelines, releases, canary releases, rollbacks, etc. This would affect the job size and scoring of the ticket.
* A deploy-only pipeline requires a specific build ID as input that will be used as a base for deployment. This introduces possible dangerous scenarios when the apply configuration is submitted, and a newly created deploy-only pipeline is waiting for the locks of an ongoing pipeline. Once locks aquired, deploy-only pipeline will override the newest version with the old one.

The alternative solution is not to use the deploy-only pipeline but to keep using “deployments” as a way to apply configuration changes. But this approach is also dangerous as it might lead to an unexpected release of the “old” version. So using a deploy-only pipeline is justified, but with the additional support of “latest version” that is acquired after the locks are taken.

My proposed solution is:

# Make it possible to redeploy “currently deployed” version with deploy-only pipelines. This would guarantee that once the deploy-only pipeline acquires locks, it will use the same version that is currently deployed:
## requires new functionality to “resolve” current version during the pipeline run (probably as a new step)
## requires changes in the deployment dashboard to allow deployment of the current version (currently, if an expected version === current version, all buttons in the deploy pipeline are disabled)
# On bulk deploy config edit apply, deploy the whole package instead of specific package services (we will notify a user of such behaviour)
# As a separate task, we will implement the deploy-only pipeline with specific selected services to not extend the scope of a current task

h2. Breakdown of Compute metrics between 15:20 and 15:35

The *18% CPU usage* between *15:20 to 15:35* strongly suggests that *only one executor* is actively working on the large partition on the worker node, while the rest of the available CPUs remain *idle*.

h3. *Worker 1: Characteristics*

# *CPU Utilization:*
#* The CPU utilization shows consistent high usage (red area) from 15:10 to 15:50, likely because it's processing the *one large partition* that is significantly larger than the others.
#* The sustained high utilization suggests that this worker is under a heavy computational load, likely dominated by tasks like shuffling, sorting, or aggregating data in that massive partition.
# *Memory Utilization:*
#* Memory usage shows steady utilization, with the "used" (blue) area remaining stable and significant caching (orange).
#* The consistent memory usage indicates that this worker might be retaining significant intermediate results or cached data related to the large partition.
# *Swap Utilization:*
#* No visible swap usage, which is good—it suggests the worker had sufficient memory allocated and avoided spilling to disk, despite the high load.

----

h3. *Workers 2-N: Characteristics*

# *CPU Utilization:*
#* CPU usage is also high from 15:10 to 15:50 but with slightly less variation compared to Worker 1.
#* This worker is likely processing the smaller partitions, leading to faster task completion and less intense sustained load.
# *Memory Utilization:*
#* Memory usage rises initially (similar to Worker 1) but stabilizes earlier. The cached memory (orange) dominates after 15:20, suggesting that this worker completed its tasks earlier and was primarily idle or handling smaller tasks for most of the job duration.
# *Swap Utilization:*
#* Like Worker 1, no swap usage is observed, indicating adequate memory resources.

----

h3. *Comparison Between Workers*

||*Aspect*||*Worker 1*||*Worker 2*||
|*Partition Load*|1 partition, *100x larger*|Many smaller partitions|
|*CPU Utilization*|High and sustained (15:10–15:50)|High but less intense overall|
|*Memory Utilization*|More consistent; large usage due to large partition|Stabilizes earlier due to smaller partitions|
|*Task Completion*|Slower, working on the large partition|Faster, finishing smaller partitions sooner|

----

h3. *Key Observations*

# *Skewed Partitioning:*
#* The *data skew* (one partition being 100x larger) caused Worker 1 to carry a disproportionate load, leading to slower task completion and higher sustained CPU/memory usage.
#* Worker 2 completed its tasks much earlier and transitioned into idle or cached states while Worker 1 continued processing the large partition.
# *Performance Bottleneck:*
#* The job's performance is bottlenecked by Worker 1, as its processing of the large partition determines the overall job completion time.

h3. *Why Does This Happen?*

This happens due to *data skew*:

* Spark assigns each partition to a single task, and tasks run independently. If one partition is much larger than others, its task will take significantly longer to complete, leaving other tasks (and their associated executors/CPUs) idle.
* In this case, the *18% utilization* likely represents one executor using its allocated CPU cores to process the large partition, while the remaining cores sit idle.

First of all, I don’t have editing rights for the attached Excel table, so I’m not sure if I should update it as well or will it be handled by your team.

Regarding the analysis, here are the key takeaways:

* Minors can only work as an employee for the fleet, not as an independent contractor. 
* There are 2 types of employment relationships: 1) standard employment based on an employment agreement; and 2) employment on the basis of an agreement on work performed outside an employment relationship.
* In the first type it is necessary to get a prior parental/legal guardian approval and the minor needs to undergo a medical examination. In the second type these are not required.



Here is the received advice in detail:

# +*Would the employment of 16-years-old persons be allowed under SK law?*+

The Slovak Law generally allows employment of minors (i. e. persons younger than 18 years). There are the two following options as to the type of the employment relationship (see A. and B. below):

*A. Standard employment based on an employment agreement* - the following general conditions apply:

i.           the minor is 15 years or older and has completed the 10-year compulsory schooling

ii.         +*the employer is obliged to ask the minor’s parent/legal guardian for a statement*+ on the minor’s employment prior conclusion of the employment agreement

* not provision of the statement, or a disagreement with the employment though does not prevent the minor from conclusion of the employment agreement. This only serves an informational purpose for the parent/legal guardian and the employer.
* the employer is advised to have a proof of sending the request for provision of the statement to the minor’s parent/legal guardian, this may be subject to inspection by the Labour Inspection Office

iii.        the minor +*must undergo a medical examination*+ prior conclusion of the employment agreement

iv.        maximum working hours of a 16 years and older employee is 37,5 hours of work / week, maximum daily working hours is 8 hours

v.          the minor must be provided with a 30-minute break after 4,5 hours of work

vi.        overtime work, night work and standby duty is not allowed

vii.      type of work must be reasonably suitable to be performed by a minor. Working conditions must not be dangerous or negatively affecting the minor’s health. Simple courier work is not specifically classified as not suitable for minors, but employers are encouraged to take more precautious health and safety measures.

 

*B. Employment on the basis of an agreement on work performed outside an employment relationship* - this is a different regime from a standard employment agreement and can be used only exceptionally. There are three types:

a. Work performance agreement – limited by max 350 hours of work / calendar year, requires a specific work task to be performed (p.e. delivery of 30 orders),

b. Agreement on work activity – limited by max 10 hours of work / week, requires a specific work activity to be performed

*c. Agreement on temporary work for students – most usually used for employment of minors*. Limited by 20 hours of work / week on average. The minor must be a high school student and provide a confirmation on the student status issued by their school. The agreement can be concluded for max 12 months, can be concluded again after the termination.

 

The general conditions from A. above apply to these contracts in B. a., b., and c., with the following exceptions:

i. the employer is not obliged to ask the minor’s parent/legal guardian for a statement on the minor’s employment

ii.  the minor does not have to undergo a medical examination, *if it is not otherwise required by law*

* the law requires medical examinations for all employees working in environment with an increased health risk. As the courier would be physically exposed to the traffic when delivering orders, *we strongly recommend the minor employee undergo the medical examination even if working on the basis of an agreement in B. a., b., or c.*

 

# +*Will this work in practice for Bolt Food delivery services? e.g. is there any requirement that parents should authorise any agreement by a 16 year old courier? or the parent's approval would be required only for the employment of the courier by the fleet / registration on the platform?*+

The parents do not authorize the agreements in A. nor B. above, the 16-year-old courier is able to sign the agreement themselves. The minor employee though cannot conclude any material liability agreement and *cannot be materially liable for damage caused to the employer’s items used for performance of work* (p. e. delivery bag, cash money if the customer pays in cash, transport vehicle). The minors also cannot conclude any commercial-like documents which would include their liability for damages or contractual penalties. *These documents also cannot be signed by their parent/legal guardian on the minor’s behalf.*

*The minor can perform the courier work only as an employee to the fleet.* Self-employment of minors is not allowed in Slovakia. The minors do not have the legal capacity to register on the Bolt platform and perform the courier work independently.

As we have the negotiation minutes, the agreement,and the repurchase agreement amendment, my take is that they were fully aware of the content of the transaction. They have the obligation to repurchase the vehicles  and correct the price in the set limits as agreed in the amendment. 

We have a similar situation with one of our other dealerships. 

Essentially, the options are as follows:

# The dealership repurchases the vehicles, pays the bank and everything is good.
# The dealership lowers the repurchase value but still repurchases the vehicles.
# The dealership refuses the repurchase, Bolt buys the vehicles and sells them, taking in the loss.
# The dealership refuses the repurchase, Bolt buys the vehicles and sells them, claiming the price difference from the dealership.
# The dealership refuses the repurchase, Bolt refuses to purchase the vehicles and Bank repos the vehicles, selling them on the market. Bank goes after the dealership for the losses.
# The dealership refuses the repurchase, Bolt refuses to purchase the vehicles and Bank repos the vehicles, selling them on the market. Bank goes after Bolt for the losses.

As a general feedback, we don’t want to sour our relationship with the bank, so *option 4* is the most likely outcome here, should the dealership completely refuse the repo.

{quote}# address data protection compliance issues (Privacy team):
## Clearly document *what data the tool collects*. I do not understand what forensic artifacts include - log files, browser history, file metadata, registry entries and temporary files? Let’s be specific.{quote}

By default nothing is collected from anyone. Collection is decided and initiated on a case by case analysis and depends on the current state of the art in forensics. This means that if we have an incident or request that requires forensic investigation, it needs to be decided based on the context. Going through the triage of the results may result in further collection requirement.

The operating systems and applications are also ever evolving, which means that the way they leave traces to the system are in constant change. At the same time forensic researchers and developers are trying to catch up. Predefining list of allowed artifacts means that by the time we have an incident and attempt to perform an investigation means that likely the list is already outdated and results will be limited.

{quote}# Conduct *a DPIA* to identify and address privacy risks before deploying the tool.
# I believe that we can rely on company’s legitimate interest as a legal basis. We will need to document that in the *LIA*.
# Revise Employees Privacy Notice if needed.{quote}

Please advise on the help needed from our side in regards to these points.

{quote}# define forensic investigation procedure (InfoSec team):
## Define types of incidents this tool is intended to address.
## Limit access to the forensic tool and the data it collects to authorised personnel only.
## Maintain detailed logs of how the tool is used and who accesses the data.{quote}

* Incidents are limited to cases where Internal Security team receives an auhtorized request or an incident with potential impact on our managed devices cannot be resolved using the endpoint detection logs. 
* As Martin Jaan commented, access to the tool can be limited to specific persons.
* The tool keeps a log of all the collections performed and who performs the collections.

{quote}# address security issues (InfoSec team):
## Conduct audit of the code before deployment
## Modify the tool, if necessary, to disable or limit the collection of personal data that is not essential.{quote}

* As Martin Jaan commented we can audit the code before deployment.
* As described earlier, by default nothing is collected and collection is only done on the selected data that is manually triggered by the investigator.

The user is reporting a double-charge because of incremental authorization.
Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. This typically happens in scenarios where the final amount of the transaction is not known upfront or may change.

I have checked the case and everything looks good on Bolt’s end. The pre-authorization has been released to the customer. 
You can ask the customer to reach out to their bank in order to confirm the authorized funds have been released. Their bank can locate the funds with the authorization date and amount.

----

*Portugal, Lisbon*

Notify the Fleet Owner (FO) when:

* The vehicle has suffered structural damage due to vandalism which could be categorised as follows:
** Parts Requiring Repair/Replacement: An event in which the damage requires repair, but has not compromised the structure of the object.
** Structural Damage Requiring Repair: An event in which the damage caused has impacted the structure of something to a moderate degree and will need to be repaired before further use.
** Equipment Unusable: An event in which the damage caused cannot be repaired.
** Unknown Damage: An event in which the damage caused cannot be determined as there is no reference to the severity of damages in the report.

During office hours, the local Operations team will inform the FO about the incident. The Operations team receives the incident notice via the OPSCRITICAL tag in the #cs-ops-carsharing-pt channel, upon submission of the Global Event Assessment Tool report.

During non-office hours and weekends, Customer Support will need to inform FO themselves. Identify the FO and inform them via call that the Roadside Assistance number was shared with the user/ or that the vehicle has suffered structural damage and describe the damage. If the FO does not answer the call, send an email instead.

Leave an internal note in the ticket that the FO was called or emailed, and informed.

Incremental authorization in card payments refers to the process of requesting an additional authorization on a customer’s card when the original authorized amount is insufficient to cover the final transaction cost. We are aware the SEB bank is not always effectively able to process the incremental authorizations. They can't link with different payments into one.

I might be wrong here. But the thing is not about throughput that can be handled by our subscribers. Technically we might be at 10% capacity. But what about system working as expected - “automating” cases?

Our MQ subscribers poll new events which means that new batch is not polled before previous completed. So, let’s assume the following scenario:

* all our subscribers are busy with handling batches and OpenAI latency is close to 1m timeout
* processing is finished and we poll for new events. But those new events are already ~1m old. Which means that we have just couple of seconds left before they will be unassigned by cron as they are already assigned to bot for 1 minute and no actions are taken.

!image-20241129-081611.png|width=1398,height=731,alt="image-20241129-081611.png"!

{quote}Maybe we can start with 1.5 minutes?{quote}

Maybe.  Based on my thinking process above, if oldest message is already ~1 minute, it’s going to be unassigned by cron in 30seconds. 

{quote}If we increase the number of parallel messages, wouldn’t we still time out if OpenAI latencies are high?
Let’s say we have 15 msgs batch and all are pending for 1 minute (for each instance). Wouldn’t it throttle anyway?{quote}

15 messages * 6 pods * 2 clusters = 160 messages is this “natural” throughput of support-bot if OpenAI latency is close to 1m timeout. So, _maybe probably_ we shouldn’t be throttled (assuming 150 messages at max from ticket description)?

This happens when driver’s compensations/campaigns are more than their commission. Since we deduct their compensations/campaigns from their commission, in that case they don’t have any commission to invoice.

The invoice is generated once their commission again exceeds their compensation/campaign/ ride discounts sum. Then this invoice would cover the whole period without an invoice.

It might poll already 10 events as we were not handling events for almost 1 minute. Age of those events already around 1m and no matter how quickly OpenAI  replies for those 10 events, _most likely_ those cases will be unassigned from Alfred by cron before? {quote}It might poll already 10 events as we were not handling events for almost 1 minute{quote}

My point is that according to the capacity metrics in Grafana, this doesn’t happen ❓🤔 Because if we have underutilized capacity then there are fewer messages that we could take. Then those 10 events would have been taken by another instance by this time. 
Unless the events are distributed evenly regardless of the instance ‘traffic’ (aka simple load balancing, modulo-like), then in theory instance could have a queue of events when another one already processed its events.
Or the batches are underutilized but the instances are not. For example, we take 6 messages per instance whereas we could take 10. Then we’re using 60% capacity, but not processing quickly enough because of latency.   

However, given that we have 150 messages per minute, it’s more likely that we’re at 100% capacity than at 10% and the 10% number should be multiplied by the parallel messages number 🤔  

Let’s try 15 parallel messages and observe the metrics, I hope we’ll have a better understanding of the capacity then (/)

h2. targeting

h3. Full context

Along with model-invoker changes we aimed to improved targeting since errors were raised there, too. We adjusted the [parallel calls from|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/pull/119394/files#diff-e0124710494f972816cd77b4bfa988c756043320694c752d5af412d079695703]:

{noformat}        max_parallel_requests: 20,
        max_elements_per_request: 10 [was the default value]{noformat}

To:

{noformat}        max_parallel_requests: 20,
        max_elements_per_request: 5{noformat}

These changes did not lead to any improvements. We also noticed the initial configuration still handled better the errors then the second approach.

I conclude that the backend likely faced the same level of concurrency but had to handle a higher number of requests overall in the new configuration, increasing the chance of bottlenecks.

h3. Proposal summary

We could try a configuration that reduces parallelism slightly to ease backend load while it maintains a reasonable payload size for efficiency:

{noformat}        max_parallel_requests: 15,
        max_elements_per_request: 10{noformat}

*Result of the initial clarification:* Given that the [comment below|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/PIF-2192?focusedCommentId=2775266] adds to the “acceptance criteria”, this ticket includes two distinct requests. Implementing them requires a detailed analysis of the problems to fully understand them. 

h2. Request 1

*Problem statement*: the current version of the {{Modal library for Backend-driven UI}} cannot enforce strict types of custom actions (defined by consumers) on the Modal’s buttons. This is possible with pure Typescript (see [Try 1|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5565120536/Extensible+APIs+with+strict+types#Try-1] in the linked document), but the API Generator cannot parse it. 

*Solution*: Two steps are needed:

* Support for generics: Start from [Try 1|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/5565120536/Extensible+APIs+with+strict+types#Try-1] and make the API Generator support it 
* Add support for a “magic” type as described in the document.

h2. Request 2

*Problem statement:* We need recursive types to describe UI using the Backend-Driven UI framework. To make the framework extensive, those recursive types should use generics (this way, each service can add its own components). Typescript itself does not support this.

*Solution*:

* The linked document describes using a “magic” generic type, which silences the TS compiler. It softens the type strictness, but the API generator can understand the intent behind this type and generate the strict type validators.

h2. WSJF Scores:

* User and Business Value: 8 (developer will use it regularly, as described in the document, not only the Modal library can benefit)
* Time Criticality: 5 (ideally implemented in one quarter)
* Opportunity enablement: 8 (API Generator is Tier 2 Component)
* Job Size: 3 (a week - as recommended for RnD tickets)
* Risk reduction: 2 (little to no risk reduction - enables stricter type validations)

* Only 1 ticket had the item already registered in the tracker prior to the interaction.

Update 29.11: 

* Latest query

{noformat}-- Step 1: Base data extraction
with base as (
    select
        at.name as event_name,
        p.email,
        from_unixtime(a.start_time) as start_time,
        from_unixtime(a.updated_at) as updated_at,
        from_unixtime(a.end_time) as end_time,
        from_unixtime(a.created_at) as created_at,
        date_diff('second', from_unixtime(a.start_time), from_unixtime(a.end_time)) as duration_seconds,
        a.description
    from ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.activity a
    join ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.activity_type at
        on a.activity_type_id = at.id
    join ng_fivetran_cs_assembled.people p
        on a.agent_id = p.agent_id
    where a._fivetran_deleted = false
),

-- Step 2: Generate hour-level ranges
hours as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        created_at,
        updated_at,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        duration_seconds,
        description,
        date_trunc('hour', start_time) as hour_start,
        date_trunc('hour', end_time) as hour_end,
        sequence(
            date_trunc('hour', start_time),
            date_trunc('hour', end_time),
            interval '1' hour
        ) as hour_intervals
    from base
),

-- Step 3: Explode hourly intervals
exploded as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        hour_interval as hour_start,
        date_add('hour', 1, hour_interval) as hour_end,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        created_at,
        updated_at
    from hours
    cross join unnest(hour_intervals) as t(hour_interval)
),

-- Step 4: Slice events to fit within hourly intervals
sliced as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        least(hour_end, end_time) as least_end_time,
        greatest(hour_start, start_time) as greatest_start_time,
        least(to_unixtime(hour_end), to_unixtime(end_time)) - 
        greatest(to_unixtime(hour_start), to_unixtime(start_time)) as hourly_duration_seconds,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        created_at,
        updated_at
    from exploded
    where hour_start < end_time
),

-- Step 5: Deduplicate rows
deduplicated as (
    select 
        email,
        event_name,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        hourly_duration_seconds,
        created_at,
        updated_at,
        row_number() over (
            partition by email, event_name, hour_start, hour_end, start_time, end_time, hourly_duration_seconds, created_at, updated_at 
            order by updated_at desc
        ) as row_num
    from sliced
),
filtered_deduplicated as (
    select *
    from deduplicated
    where row_num = 1
),

-- Step 6: Detect overlapping events within the same hour with latest updates
overlaps_resolved as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        hourly_duration_seconds,
        created_at,
        updated_at,
        max(updated_at) over (
            partition by email, event_name, hour_start, hour_end
        ) as max_updated_at_hourly_event_level,
        max(updated_at) over (
            partition by email, hour_start, hour_end
        ) as max_updated_at_hourly,
        case 
            when exists (
                select 1
                from filtered_deduplicated f2
                where f2.email = f1.email
                and f2.hour_start = f1.hour_start
                and f2.hour_end = f1.hour_end
                and f2.start_time < f1.end_time
                and f2.end_time > f1.start_time
                and f2.updated_at != f1.updated_at
            ) then 1
            else 0
        end as is_overlapping
    from filtered_deduplicated f1
    where hour_start < end_time
),

-- Step 7: Filter out overlapping events
filtered as (
    select
        email,
        event_name,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        hourly_duration_seconds,
        created_at,
        updated_at,
        max_updated_at_hourly_event_level,
        max_updated_at_hourly,
        is_overlapping
    from overlaps_resolved
    where 
        is_overlapping = 0 or
        (is_overlapping = 1 and updated_at = max_updated_at_hourly)
),

-- Step 8: Aggregate durations by event type
final as (
    select
        email,
        hour_start,
        hour_end,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Queue' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as queue_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Break' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as break_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Day Off' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as day_off_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Social Media' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as social_media_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Other' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as other_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Vacation' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as vacation_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Offline Tasks' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as offline_tasks_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Special Leave' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as special_leave_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Training' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as training_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Price Review' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as pr_duration,
        sum(case when event_name = 'Overtime' then hourly_duration_seconds end) as overtime_duration
    from filtered
    group by email, hour_start, hour_end
)


select *
from final
limit 100{noformat}

We have *documented this incident internally* to ensure accountablility.

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

Hi [~accountid:5f0c30effe23000022252e68] please see below my thoughts:

*What are scheduled rides?*

The Scheduled Rides feature enables Riders to book a ride in advance. A user will be able to reserve a trip up to 3 days in advance and at least 30 minutes in advance.

If a user requests a trip in the future, a driver will be assigned in advance of the trip time. Once an order is placed, the trip fare is locked and will not change (additional costs due to destination change during the trip or additional driver waiting time might be charged). The driver will arrive in advance and will wait for a passenger for 15 minutes free of charge.

Since a driver will be reserved in advance, trip cancellation less than 1 hour before pick-up will result in a cancellation fee to be paid to the fleet (minus the intermediation fee). 

The price is higher in this type of service:

||*Standard Ride*||*Scheduled Ride*||
|!image-20241129-151237.png|width=33.333333333333336%,alt="image-20241129-151237.png"!|!image-20241129-151319.png|width=391,height=632,alt="image-20241129-151319.png"!|

*What is the problem?*

There are rumours that some Drivers use apps to automatically accept scheduled rides and then cancel if they are not interested. Riders are paying extra for reliability. Some countries have enrolment criteria for Drivers to ensure quality. We would like to implement similar criteria but would like to do it in a way to mitigate the reclassification risk.

Introducing quality criteria increases the risk of reclassification namely for the following reasons:

* One of the reclassification criteria in PT is the power of direction: “_The platform exercises power of direction and determines specific rules, in particular with regard to i) the way the activity provider presents itself,  ii) its conduct towards the service user or iii)_ *_the provision of the activity_*”
* For this reason, in 2023 driver quality criteria associated to some categories has been removed (e.g. Executive).
* The current project would reintroduce driver quality criteria associated with scheduled rides, for the same reasons there were such criteria in the past related with premium categorias.

*How could we mitigate the reclassification risk?*

* *Defining reasonable criteria that incentivise compliance with the TVDE law INSTEAD OF determining specific behaviour rules or verifying quality of the service*
** TVDE law determines that TVDE services may only be refused if they: a) Involve travelling on roads that are clearly impassable due to difficult access or in places that pose a notorious danger to the safety of the vehicle, passengers or driver; b) Are requested by people with suspiciously dangerous behaviour; c) Are requested in a manner incompatible with the provisions of this law.
** The criteria established are *based on rides that the driver first accepts and then, for some reason (cancellation, fraud), doesn’t finish*, leaving the rider unattended
*** *Minimum Finished Rate (%)*: Threshold to be defined, meaning they indeed finish the rides they first accept.
*** *Maximum Number of Unfulfilled Scheduled Rides in the Last 12 Weeks:* Threshold to be defined. Please note that an “unfulfilled scheduled ride” refers to instances where the driver accepts the ride, begins driving, and then cancels.
** When defining the KPIs please consider that the threshold in the t&c regarding the illegitimate refusal of services is 30% of rides: _“1.12. É o Operador TVDE que determina quando presta Serviços de Transporte, de tal forma que poderá aceitar, legitimamente recusar ou ignorar Serviços de Transporte, sem prejuízo das regras relativas à recusa de serviço, previstas no artigo 8.º da Lei n.º 45/2018, de 10 de agosto._ *_A recusa de pedidos de serviços iguais ou superiores a 30 por cento ou mais dos serviços comunicados presume-se não conforme com o artigo supracitado._* _O Operador TVDE é, no entanto, obrigado a prestar Serviços de Transporte depois de o Motorista que atue em sua representação ter aceitado transportar o Utilizador desde o ponto de recolha até ao ponto de destino, sem prejuízo de circunstâncias imprevistas (p.ex., uma avaria mecânica).”_
* Drivers will not be blocked or excluded from operating TVDE services in the platform in case of non-compliance with the KPIS. Alternatively, drivers will be *temporarily suspended from accessing to scheduled rides access* only. Additionally, drivers regain access as soon as they meet the criteria again.

*Summary:*

* IMO we have put in place measures to ensure minimisation of reclassification risks, but the risk of reclassification remains given that there is a specific reclassification law in Portugal for platform workers.
* The KPIs suggested to ensure drivers act autonomous and independently. A further measures to ensure such autonomy to be considered would be ensuring the access to scheduled rides can be decided on by the driver or fleet (either by allowing opt-in or opt-out).

Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Thank you.

h1. Clarification

There are many risks and complexities associated with changes that span across multiple packages:

* the code review requires approval from multiple teams
* the deployment needs to lock all the packages, resulting in:
** long waiting time before being able to deploy such a change
** locking others from deploying those packages for a long time
* it takes lots of time to build and test the code
* the chance of getting a failed test is much higher
* due to various cross-package dependencies, it gets complex to figure out and execute the required order of deployment and rollback
* +last but not least+, the Builder selects all packages by default when common files are touched — the Builder will likely crash trying to run it

We want engineers to avoid those problems by not deploying many packages simultaneously.
However, we don’t want to block bigger releases — sometimes they are necessary.

We will add a soft warning to the Builder UI to achieve that.

The Builder frontend application already has all the data needed to issue such warnings: all the packages and selected packages. So no backend changes will be needed.

So mostly, the task executing will be about deciding the numeric threshold(s) and alert message text(s).

One idea is to have two thresholds,

* a smaller one for a warning like this:

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
You selected more than X packages for deployment! Be aware of the following risks:

* …
* …
* …
{panel}

* a bigger one for a more critical warning when all (or almost all, and bigger than X) packages are selected:

{panel:bgColor=#ffebe6}
Too many packages are selected for deployment. Reach out to #dev-pint-support before starting this.
{panel}

(the texts are indicative, to be fixed during the actual task implementation)

Potentially, this setting is not needed as we can invert the default value from false to true (driver would be able to select categories by default). More context here [https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02LWCMELDD/p1731419986295039?thread_ts=1730990847.346779&cid=C02LWCMELDD|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C02LWCMELDD/p1731419986295039?thread_ts=1730990847.346779&cid=C02LWCMELDD|smart-link]

BrightHire enables clients to determine their data retention periods. Candidate data retention settings in BrightHire can be synced to existing Greenhouse settings to ensure consistency. Client BrightHire admins can execute data deletion to honor candidate deletion requests. So, the retention periods in BrightHire should mirror our retention periods - this is the best approach, I think. 

Consent functionally in the ongoing interview:

# Recording notification: all interview participants are notified of the recording at the the outset of the interview, and this notification can be customized by the customer
# Interviewer Controls: Pause, resume or stop recording at any time from the BrightHire app during a video, phone, or in-person interview.
# Easily Remove the Notetaker: Interviewers can stop recording any time by removing the notetaker.
# Candidate notification: Candidates are notified when recording is paused or stopped.

*In addition:* 

# Data minimization: BrightHire only processes the minimum amount of personal data over the minimum period of time required to provide the Service.
# Data subject requests: BrightHire provides technical and organizational assistance to clients to help respond to inquiries from data subjects who wish to exercise their privacy rights. For example, BrightHire assists clients in responding to requests to access, correct, or delete personal data. If a client receives a privacy request from a candidate, the client should contact BrightHire. If BrightHire receives a privacy request from a candidate, BrightHire will contact the client first to receive written instructions on how to proceed. BrightHire will deliver GDPR compliant data to a client to enable them to respond to data requests.
# Notification and opt-out collection: The Platform enables clients to send automated notices to inform users of recorded interviews and to provide users the ability to seamlessly opt-out of clients' use of BrightHire both before an interview as
well as while an interview is taking place.
# Opt-in consent collection: If a client chooses to collect explicit opt-in consent for processing, BrightHire works with the client to set up its online application to capture explicit consent and to have the client’s ATS seamlessly instruct Brighthire
to join and record the interview. It also enables clients to select at the interviewer-level whether or not Brighthire should join an interview based on whether or not the interviewer has provided consent.

Dear Doros,

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *29 October 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

* If you can see a task with an error message _Invoice sum too small_: The invoice was not generated as the driver did not owe any commission to Bolt or he had more compensation than owed commission

FOR NOV as you can see: -419.87

That’s because their commission amount is negative, meaning we don’t have any commission to invoice.

This happens when driver’s compensations/campaigns are more than their commission. Since we deduct their compensations/campaigns from their commission, in that case they don’t have any commission to invoice.

The invoice is generated once their commission again exceeds their compensation/campaign/ ride discounts sum. Then this invoice would cover the whole period without an invoice.

Here a quick try on how to calculate it:

In OCT it was -157.9 

Aggregated data for Nov:



!image-20241202-132513.png|width=75%,alt="image-20241202-132513.png"!

Commission for NOV in total: 110.72 + 337.15 = 447.87

commission - bonuses = 447.87 - 706.96 = -259.09

OCT ( - 157.9) + Nov (-259.09) = - 416.99 → That is quick approx calculation for you to understand, couple EUR diff probably is coming from Rider discounts

{noformat}WITH unique_packages AS (
    SELECT 
        id,
        approx_distinct(json_extract_scalar(l, '$.name')) AS unique_package_count
    FROM ng_platform.builder_build_action
    CROSS JOIN UNNEST(try(CAST(json_parse(locks) AS ARRAY(JSON)))) AS t(l)
    WHERE 
        json_extract_scalar(l, '$.is_service') = 'true' AND
        json_extract_scalar(l, '$.name') LIKE '%env:live%' and
        json_extract_scalar(l, '$.name') LIKE '%app:1;%' AND
        created >= current_timestamp - INTERVAL '365' DAY
    GROUP BY id
) SELECT 
    MAX(unique_package_count) AS max_packages,
    AVG(unique_package_count) AS avg_packages,
    APPROX_PERCENTILE(unique_package_count, 0.5) AS median_packages,
    APPROX_PERCENTILE(unique_package_count, 0.70) AS p70_packages,
    APPROX_PERCENTILE(unique_package_count, 0.95) AS p95_packages,
    APPROX_PERCENTILE(unique_package_count, 0.99) AS p99_packages
FROM unique_packages;
{noformat}

The additional suggested spend *5.5K* was out of the budget so I proposed to limit the experiment to *10 days* but keep the maximum possible level of spend. Strictly speaking, additional spend of *3K* didn’t result in statistically significant signups, but when I was analyzing the plot I noticed that cumulative effect almost broke through the MDE baseline on the 10th day. I think that would be conclusive if we run it for a couple of more days.
* [2024-10 Prague Google iOS drop|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/5626102727/2024-10+Prague+Google+iOS+drop] - *no incrementality.* A drop from *1500* to *280* daily didn’t result in statistically significant signup drop. I checked the last year experiment with [Google iOS launch|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/4737990849/2023-11+Prague+Google+iOS+Launch] - it didn’t show any result either (it was done on FTRs though). Seems like Google iOS has a very low efficiency in that market. 
* [2024-10 Bratislava Google iOS increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/5628788917/2024-10+Bratislava+Google+iOS+increase] - *no incrementality.* Increased spend from 200 to 420 daily didn’t result in statistically significant uplift in signups. At some point it was close to detect a negative impact. The Android/iOS relationship was not stable during the experiment period for some reason (there was an unexpected spike in Android signups right before the end of the experiment).
* [2024-10 Madrid Tiktok iOS launch|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/5631180905/2024-10+Madrid+Tiktok+iOS+launch] - *no incrementality.* Change of spend from 350 to 1030 daily didn’t result in statistically significant increase in signups, not even close. There was a “small incrementality” during a couple of days right after the experiment launch which then vanished for the rest of the period
* [2024-10 Birmingham Google iOS increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/5631541480/2024-10+Birmingham+Google+iOS+increase] - *no incrementality.* Increase in spend from 450 to 1300 daily was no sufficient to conclude a stable long-term incrementality. There was an impact detected during the first week of experiment, however it didn’t last long for some reason.
* [2024-10 Krakow Meta iOS reach launch |https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/5633146911/2024-10+Krakow+Meta+iOS+launch]- *no incrementality.* Launch of the Meta iOS channel with budget almost twice bigger than suggested didn’t result in statistically significant increase in signups. Channel is considered to have a very low efficiency.
* [2024-11 Warsaw Tiktok iOS reach increase|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/MP/pages/5632262294/2024-11+Warsaw+Tiktok+iOS+reach+increase] - *inconclusive.* Increase in Tiktok reach spend from 230 to 1080 resulted in statistically significant decrease in signups, which obviously violates our main positive impact assumption. Dear Anna,

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *10 November 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

{quote}If you cannot find instructions from the Knowledge Base for solving the case, leave a comment in the internal notes of the ticket before escalating to Tier 2 or OPS:

* A brief description of the issue
* The investigation completed so far, including a link to the KB article that does not have the answer needed to solve the issue
* All relevant ticket, user profile, and order links
* The question that needs to be answered or the reason for the escalation.{quote}

Due to them explicitly covering only situations when an agent can’t find instructions from the KB for solving the case, I added a sentence in the *“Cases that should always be escalated to Tier 2 agents“* section that agents should always add an internal note with a brief description and what assistance is required from Tier 2 when escalating a case. The section on escalations to OPS already contains this instruction. 



So, to conclude - even though I’ve made some minor adjustments to make the instructions more explicit, I'd say that from a content perspective, the relevant information and guidelines were already there, so it looks more like a process adherence issue on the agent side. 💭

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on *4 November 2024.*

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software. Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail, we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about *you* which you are entitled. This includes:

* *Order History*

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|https://bolt.eu/en-gb/privacy/|smart-link], which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,

 

Bolt

*Estimated timeline and suggested procedure from Wiersholm*: 

Wiersholm suggest filing for an *interim measure (injunction)* at the *same time (and in the same document) as the statement of claim*, but to argue for a separate hearing related to the injunction. The purpose of the injunction is to restrain the entering into effect of the new legislation, until the Court of First Instance has decided on the case (on the basis of a decision by the EFTA-court).   

+Possible timeline:+

* File statement of claim/injunction – mid December 2024
* Government's reply to injunction – first week of January 2025
* Oral hearing injunction – mid/late January 2025
* Decision on injunction – early/mid February 2025

The Court's decision as to the injunction can be appealed. As a main rule, this entails a written proceeding before the Court of Appeals, but we can argue for an oral hearing and expect this to be granted. If so, a hearing should be scheduled around early April, and a decision be handed down at the end of that month. The timeline would probably be more or less the same under a written procedure. While the Court of First Instance handles cases concerning injunctions quickly, we should note that there is more uncertainty as to the timeline before the Court of Appeals.    

* Main case, decision regarding request for advisory opinion to the EFTA Court, late January/early February 2025 (the Government will clearly argue against this)
* Questions submitted to the EFTA Court, late February 2025 (this could take more time, as the Government usually tries to obstruct the process with long discussions on the questions to be submitted)
* Oral hearing at the EFTA Court, possibly in June but more likely in September 2025 or even later in the autumn (this depend to a significant degree on the case load at the Court).
* Decision by the EFTA Court, probably around November 2025. Based on statistics from the EFTA-court, it will normally take from 8-12 months from the questions are submitted by the national court to the decision is handed down.  

+The process before the EFTA Court can be briefly summarized as follows+:

* The process begins with the national court sending the request for an advisory opinion to the EFTA Court. This document is traditionally written in Norwegian.
* The request is translated into English by the EFTA Court.
* The EFTA Court sends the request, in both Norwegian and English versions, to the parties involved in the national proceedings, the EFTA Surveillance Authority (ESA), the European Commission, and all EEA states.
* All recipients have the same absolute deadline—two months from the dispatch of the request—to submit written observations in the case.
* In practice, submissions are almost always made by the parties, the EFTA Surveillance Authority (ESA), and the European Commission, and to varying degrees by the individual EEA states. In this case, as discussed, a submission from Estonia would be very valuable.
* It is normally not possible to submit additional written observations to the EFTA Court.
* A few months after the deadline for written submissions has passed, a brief oral hearing is held before the EFTA Court, where the parties in the case typically have 30 minutes each for their presentations, while other participants usually have 15 minutes.
* Before the oral hearing, the EFTA Court prepares a report for the hearing. The report provides a summary of the legal and factual aspects of the case and of the written submissions to the EFTA Court.
* The EFTA Courts advisory opinion is sent to the national court, the parties and the other participants in the case
* Hearing in Norway, Court of First Instance, December 2025.
* Decision by the court, late December/early January (2026)

The court's decision can be appealed within one month, and a hearing before the Court of Appeals will normally be scheduled within six to eight months. For the sake of completeness, Wiersholm note that the Court of Appeals' decision can be appealed to the Supreme Court, but will only be admitted to a hearing here if the case is deemed to be of significant general interest (this will probably apply in the present case). Again, the timeframe is ca. six months from appeal to hearing.

+When will the case be public:+

* Due to the request for an injunction, the case will probably be public as soon as the first hearing is scheduled and at least when the hearing is held.

+What Wiersholm need from Bolt:+

* Wiersholm have most of what they need to start drafting, on the basis of the complaint to ESA and the material submitted to the Competition Authority
* Nevertheless, a meeting (as scheduled) to go through the facts relating to the structure of the business in more detail will be very valuable (will be held December 3, 2024)

*Further – it is important to note that an interim measure (injunction) can only be granted on the following conditions under section 34-1 of the Norwegian Dispute Act*:

_(1) Interim measure may be granted:_

a. _when the defendant's conduct makes it necessary to provisionally secure the claim because the action or execution of the claim would otherwise be considerably impeded, or_

b. _when it is necessary to make a temporary arrangement in a disputed legal issue in order_ *_to avert considerable loss or inconvenience_*_, or to avoid violence which the conduct of the defendant gives reason to fear_.

_(2) An interim measure cannot be granted if the loss or inconvenience to the defendant is clearly disproportionate to the interests of the claimant in the interim measure being granted._

It follows clearly from case law that the possibility of obtaining damages at a later stage, is an argument against the fulfilment of the requirements set out above. In our experience, this is always invoked by the Government.

The Borgarting Court of Appeals summarized the case law on this matter as follows in a decision from 2018 (LB-2018-4746, AI translation):

_The requirement for grounds for security in section 34-1, first paragraph (b) of the Dispute Act indicates a complex assessment, which includes, among other things, how important the disputed legal relationship is for the plaintiff, how great a need the plaintiff has for a temporary injunction, how invasive a temporary injunction will be, the defendant's conduct, etc. cf. Rt-2002-108._ *_Where the damage or inconvenience claimed is of a financial nature, the possibility of claiming damages may lead to the alleged damage not being considered significant, or justify that an injunction is not necessary_*_. Reference is made to Rt-1996-1625, Rt-1999-1220 and LB-2008-183125. However, if the loss is difficult to calculate or pursue, or_ *_if there are other significant adverse effects other than financial ones, an injunction may still be necessary_*_, cf. Flock page 103 with references to case law. The possibility of submitting a claim for compensation will be one of several factors in the overall assessment that must be made of whether a temporary arrangement is necessary to prevent significant damage or inconvenience. The Court of Appeal cannot see that it raises problems in relation to EEA law's principle of effectiveness to attach importance to the possibility of claiming damages when assessing whether there are grounds for security, see, inter alia, C-432/05 Unibet, in particular the Advocate General's Opinion_.

*Consequently, to succeed with the injunction it is crucial that Bolt is able to show that the entering into force of the legislation will not only lead to a direct economic loss that can be claimed from the Government in a later case*. Wiersholm has therefore suggested that Bolt should start working on the above-mentioned issue. Off the top of Wiersholm’s head, possible arguments could relate to loss of drivers, loss of market penetration (brand value) etc..

We've also noticed a reduction in the demand for EU hosting recently and the primary factor to that has been the adequacy decision granted by the European Commission to United States companies participating in the EU US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) fka Privacy Shield, such as ourselves (*[https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection/adequacy-decisions_en|https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/data-protection/international-dimension-data-protection/adequacy-decisions_en|smart-link] *). As mentioned above, MentorcliQ complies with the Data Privacy Framework and copies of MentorcliQ's certifications can be found on the DPF website:* [https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/list|https://www.dataprivacyframework.gov/list|smart-link]  *In summation, we can certainly move forward with both the contractual and due diligence processes with either US or EU hosting in scope and we hope the above context proves to be helpful in those two tracks.*

[LV Public Procurement Law|https://likumi.lv/ta/id/287760-publisko-iepirkumu-likums] states that if amendments were made, the tender submission deadline should be prolonged. Below LV and ENG law text

* 35 (3) Pasūtītājs var izdarīt grozījumus iepirkuma procedūras dokumentos, ja vien grozītie noteikumi nepieļauj atšķirīgu piedāvājumu iesniegšanu vai citu kandidātu vai pretendentu dalību vai izvēli iepirkuma procedūrā. *Ja iepirkuma procedūras dokumentos izdarīti grozījumi,* *piedāvājumu iesniegšanas termiņš tiek pagarināts* atbilstoši informācijas vai izmaiņu svarīgumam *tā, lai piegādātāji vai kandidāti varētu iepazīties ar visu informāciju, kas nepieciešama piedāvājuma sagatavošanai*, un ievērojot Ministru kabineta noteiktos minimālos pieteikumu un piedāvājumu iesniegšanas termiņus.
* ENG 35(3)(3) The contracting authority may make amendments to the procurement procedure documents, provided that the amended provisions do not allow for submission of different tenders or participation or selection of other candidates or tenderers in the procurement procedure. *If the amendments have been made* to the procurement procedure documents, the *term for submission of tenders shall be extended* according to the relevance of information or changes *so that the economic operators or candidates would be able to get acquainted with all the information needed to prepare tenders,* and taking into account the minimum terms for submission of applications and tenders stipulated by the Cabinet.

Further, [the Cabinet Regulation No 107 on Tendering Procedures for Procurement Procedures and Design Contests|https://likumi.lv/ta/id/289086-iepirkuma-proceduru-un-metu-konkursu-norises-kartiba], as [@marcis.bakis|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U073FC0437E] mentioned provides 7 days extension if tender docs were adjusted. 7 days shall start running from the day the updated docs were re-published. Not sure if this was done by them. Below LV and ENG law text

* 33. Ja iepirkuma komisija *izdara grozījumus iepirkuma procedūras dokumentos*, *pieteikumu iesniegšanas minimālais termiņš pēc dienas, kad paziņojums par līgumu atkārtoti publicēts* Iepirkumu uzraudzības biroja tīmekļvietnē vai nosūtīts Eiropas Savienības Publikāciju birojam publicēšanai Eiropas Savienības Oficiālajā Vēstnesī, ir vismaz puse no sākotnēji noteiktā pieteikumu iesniegšanas termiņa, bet *ne īsāks par septiņām dienām.*
* 33. If the procurement commission *makes amendments to the procurement procedure documents*, *the minimum term for the submission of applications after the day when the contract notice is re-published* on the website of the Procurement Monitoring Bureau or sent to the Publications Office of the European Union for publication in the Official Journal of the European Union shall be at least half of the initially specified term for the submission of applications, however, *not shorter than seven days.*
