The latest version from 29.11.2024 – Partner proposes joint controllership

*Explanation:* a definition of joint controllership and assertion that the situation fits joint controllership

*Action:* pushed back and explained our position of separate data controller

{quote}Bolt cannot agree to the proposed text by Carrefour. Bolt and Carrefour did not enter into a partnership regarding the availability to the general public of products provided by Carrefour through Bolt Food Platform.

According to the Section 2 of the General Terms: For the sale of Goods through the Bolt Food Platform, a Sales Agreement is concluded directly between the Client and the Partner. For the delivery of the Order, the Client enters into a Delivery Agreement directly with the Delivery Partner. By operating the Bolt Food Platform, Bolt acts only as a provider of the information society service and is neither a party to the Sales Agreement or the Delivery Agreement. Bolt is not the provider of the Goods or delivery services.{quote}

&

{quote}Bolt's Privacy Team considers Bolt and the Partner as separate data controllers when processing personal data in the context of Bolt Food. Under the GDPR, a controller is an entity that determines the purposes ("why") and means ("how") of personal data processing. For two entities to be considered joint controllers, they must share the same purposes and means of processing.

In the case of Bolt Food, the purposes differ:

* Bolt processes customer data primarily to provide the Bolt Food platform as an information society service to both customers and the Partner. This establishes Bolt as a controller, as it independently determines its purpose for processing.
* Partner processes customer data to fulfill sales agreements (e.g., preparing and selling food). These agreements are solely between the customer and the Partner, with Bolt not being a party. The Partner's purposes for processing personal data are distinct and independent from Bolt’s, making it a separate controller.

Since both Bolt and the Partner process personal data for different purposes and make their own decisions about the processing, they cannot be considered joint controllers under GDPR. Each party operates independently within their respective roles as controllers.{quote}

Hello [~accountid:61027996fc68c1006995f1d5] , hope you’re doing well 🙂 

Only in countries with MTPL coverage (Insurance that indemnifies for damages caused to other persons or their property by the vehicle) damages to third-party properties are covered (see [KB|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/99832?country=global&language=en#liability-exceptions], there is also a table with country-specific coverage details). 

!Screenshot 2024-12-03 at 11.02.45.png|width=855,height=93,alt="Screenshot 2024-12-03 at 11.02.45.png"!

So if the accident happens where there is MTPL (for example, Norway), the insurance form link will show up, even if you select YES, because the MTPL coverage overrides the conditions listed in the tool. 

!Screenshot 2024-12-03 at 11.08.24.png|width=276,height=716,alt="Screenshot 2024-12-03 at 11.08.24.png"!

For countries without the MTPL (the majority of them), if you select YES, it means that one of the conditions listed applies, so the insurance form link won’t show up (because insurance won’t cover damages to third parties). 

!Screenshot 2024-12-03 at 11.09.00.png|width=272,height=731,alt="Screenshot 2024-12-03 at 11.09.00.png"!

Hope it’s clear. Let me know if you have further questions. 

Cheers, 

Alessandro

Thank you for your data subject rights request, which we received on 5 November 2024.

*(1) Copy of your personal data*

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, the law requires a data controller such as ourselves to protect the rights of third parties (including the rights of drivers and Bolt employees). Furthermore, we must point out that we are not required to disclose documents or otherwise provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

You have the right to request rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing of personal data concerning you or to object to such processing. If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. Yours sincerely,

Hey [~accountid:712020:7f47c2af-14e1-4206-a795-ac87cb906276] the central product pricing team is picking this up. Your local team should reach out to @giammarco pavan. 
Generally every fixed fee (besides cancellation fee) we are trying to hide need to be reflected in all the other components which need to be available. e.g. Start rate being hidden in the rate card but need to be reflected in the price per km or price per minute or a combination of both. We have moved away from the disclaimer situation. 

This is the following advise we have given on how to hide the start rate to the Product Pricing team:

# *Integration into kilometer price:*

* Increase price per km from 6.10 kr/KM
* Distribute “Start” component across average trip distance
* Advantage: Simple, transparent pricing structure
* Note: Requires analysis of average trip lengths

# *Adjustment of minute price:*

* Increase from current 4.64 kr/MIN
* Integrate “Start” component based on average trip duration
* Transparent display for consumers

# *Combination approach:*

* Split between km and minute prices
* Enables balanced pricing
* Minimizes extreme price changes

*Key legal considerations*:

* Clear display of price components
* Final price display must include all costs
* Pricing calculation must be comprehensible to consumers
* Documentation of pricing methodology for potential regulatory inquiries

That’s the rate card strategy the Product Team has built considering our assessment and advise: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PCC-0KUW4TrTUwHs49htPLbl6ThRWPP4ykFtwchbiIc/edit?tab=t.0|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1PCC-0KUW4TrTUwHs49htPLbl6ThRWPP4ykFtwchbiIc/edit?tab=t.0|smart-link]

Hello hello, 

* PA - Riders’ Personal Accident. This covers the rider if they injure themselves or suffer a fatality (during a ride). 
* RGL - Riders’ General Liability - covers the rider for any damages they may cause to someone’s property or body (during a ride).
* MTPL - Motor Third Party Liability - covers the rider for any damages they may cause to someone’s property or body (including stationary vehicle). 

Where we have MTPL, we send the claim to the insurer in any case. 

Where we don't have MTPL, we send them out only if the user did not breach T&C

----

So, RGL does not cover if:

*One of these applies:* 

* User was *under 18* years old during the accident
* User was *tandem riding* 
     _◦ More than one person used the e-vehicle at the same time_
* User was *under the influence* of alcohol or drugs, before or during the ride
* User was driving *recklessly/dangerously*
     *_◦_* _Example: Wheelies, Drifting, etc._
* User *unsafely carried goods/cargo*
     _◦ Examples: Bag hung from the handlebar, box on the deck, etc._
* E-vehicle was *used for commercial purposes*, e.g. Food Delivery

----

User’s *personal property was damaged*
     _◦ Examples: Cracked phone screen, broken glasses, etc._

* User received *small injuries*
     _◦ Examples: Small cuts, minor/heavy bruising, muscle soreness, moral damages, broken fingers, 1-2 missing teeth, smaller bone fractures, etc._

----

* Damage to property or injury occurred *from a parked scooter* (not in use by user) - This is covered only by MTPL

----

h1. Modeling importance of overlaps – Iteration #1

h2. Conclusion

_Potentially overlapping_ _campaigns_ explain *little* portion of variance in the errors of the current model. There can be two reasons for it:

# Uninformative features. _Potential_ overlaps don’t yet mean that a user gets enrolled into multiple campaigns simultaneously. A better approach would be to extract the precise historical data from enrollments — possibility & effort estimation TBD;
# Errors are affected by other factors, like targeting rules. These factors may interfere with effects from overlaps.

----

h2. 1. Data Preparation

Campaigns might overlap if:

* Active at the same time
* In the same location (country of city)
* Same bonus type (% on delivery or food)
* NOT (same_test & same_bonus_type & different bundle)


For each campaign, I calculated the number of potentially overlapping *campaign-days*. Suppose we have three campaigns:

||*M*||*T*||*W*||*T*||*F*||*S*||*S*||
|X|X|X|X|X|X|X|
|X| | |X| | | |
|X| | | | | |X|

For campaigns #1, #2 and #3 the number of overlapping campaign-days would be 4, 3 and 3 respectively.

Then for each campaign I also aggregated the info on *bonuses* of it’s potentially overlapping campaigns: mean, median, std, max. 



h2. 2. Error prediction

I tried to predict the current model’s *errors* on food-discounting campaigns with the following features with an XGB model:

!download-4.png|width=100%,alt="download-4.png"!

{{spend_target_absolute}} – Output value of the current model. Can be thought of as a distillation of all the previous knowledge about given campaign.

{{bonus_data_percentage}} – Discount value of the campaign.

{{y}} (target) – campaign’s [symmetric absolute percentage error|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symmetric_mean_absolute_percentage_error]. 

*Why sMAPE as a target*

At first I tried to predict APE, but due to its unbounded nature the results were very poor (negative r2). Since sMAPE is bounded in range [0, 2], the prediction task got much easier

*Why only food discount campaigns*

The info on bonuses of potentially overlapping campaigns is only useful for campaigns that discount food – delivery is always discounted at 100% rate. If we try to explain delivery campaigns with overlaps, we only get r2=0.24.

*What if we add a feature `previous_campaigns_in_city`*

{{previous_campagns_in_city}} – The number of campaigns in the same city before the current one. This is a proxy for model’s _learning opportunity_ at the time of prediction – although the current model is trained on all the data, discarding city identities and only using their GMV. Also this feature indirectly captures the _market size and activity_.
Adding this feature improves R^2^ 0.44 → 0.48.
This is also expectedly correlated (0.25) with {{overlap_campaign_days}}. But curiously, it almost doesn’t change its SHAP values:
!download-5.png|width=100%,alt="download-5.png"!
Based on the interaction between the two, we might _speculate_ that higher volumes of historical data may partially offset overlapping effects — i.e. the model could learn to underestimate certain campaigns in advance — but the data is too noisy for such a claim.
!download-6.png|width=100%,alt="download-6.png"!


*Overlap features correlation*

The more {{overlap_campaign_days}}, the higher {{overlap_bonus_mean}} and the lower {{overlap_bonus_std}}
!download-9.png|width=91.66666666666669%,alt="download-9.png"!


The model was able to explain some variance in error, but didn’t perform very well, especially with high actual errors:

!newplot (1).png|width=66.66666666666666%,alt="newplot (1).png"!

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
Keep in mind that r2=0.44 is together with the {{spend_target_absolute}} feature, i.e. the output value from the previous model. Without it we only get r2=0.19 at errors prediction; and _only with_ it (w/o overlap features) r2=0.17. 

So the high-level *overlap modeling explains something, but not much*.
{panel}

SHAP values do not offer any revelations:

* Campaigns with lower original estimates tend to have lower errors;
* When std of bonuses from potentially overlapping campaigns is low, the error is lower;
* When current campaign’s discount is low, the error is higher and vice-versa.

!download-7.png|width=100%,alt="download-7.png"!

The influence of overlap features is still very noisy:

!download-10.png|width=50%,alt="download-10.png"!

!download-8.png|width=50%,alt="download-8.png"!
